of its own: no download accepts it, and the API browser accepts no other kind. A user holds
at most three unused ones; a fourth is refused, with nothing audited, until one of them is
used or lapses. Any signed-in user may ask while the Developer setting serves the API browser.
Audited as `ApiBrowserOpened`.

post.summary: Log in and issue a session token
post.description:
Anonymous. Unknown-user and wrong-password cases are deliberately indistinguishable (same 401,
same message, matched hash-verification timing); the distinction lives only in the audit log.
If the account is valid but held pending a password change (admin-forced or policy-expired),
no token is issued: the 200 body carries `PasswordChangeRequired` and a `Reason`, and
the client should run the forced-change flow.

requestBody.description: The login credentials

200.description: Either an issued session token, a `PasswordChangeRequired` marker directing the client to the forced-change flow, or a `PasskeyRequired` marker when the account must sign in with its passkey

401.description: Invalid credentials, or the account is suspended

429.description: This address has had too many failed sign-in attempts

post.summary: Finish a sign-in with a recovery code in place of the passkey it owes
post.description:
A recovery code is the way back in when passkeys are REQUIRED and the passkey is gone.
It is single-use, and spending one is audited at Security severity because it is either
a bad day or an intrusion, and both want looking at.

requestBody.description: The original credentials plus the recovery code

200.description: An issued session token, or a `PasswordChangeRequired` marker when the account is held pending a password change

401.description: The password or the code was wrong, or the account is suspended

429.description: This address has had too many failed sign-in attempts

post.summary: Extend the caller's session
post.description:
Reissues a token for the SAME session with a fresh expiry. The client calls this on a
timer while the app is open, so an active user is never dumped back to the login screen
mid-task. Not audited: it is a mechanical refresh of an existing sign-in, not a new one,
and on a timer it would bury the log. The sign-in itself is already recorded, and
revoking the session still ends it - a renewal cannot resurrect a killed session.
Open to an enrolment-only session, which renews with the enrolment scope it was
created with: renewing extends a session, it never widens one.

200.description: A replacement token and its new expiry

401.description: Not authenticated, or the session has been revoked or expired

post.summary: Confirm the caller's password from a live session
post.description:
The sensitive self-service actions (new recovery codes, a passkey added or removed)
require a credential proved within the last few minutes, so a bearer token that was
lifted cannot be turned into a lasting foothold. This records a password proof on the
caller's session; a passkey assertion does the same through the passkey endpoints.
Throttled like a sign-in, because it verifies a password like one.

requestBody.description: The caller's current password

204.description: The proof was recorded on the session

401.description: The password was wrong, or the session has ended

429.description: This address has had too many failed sign-in attempts

post.summary: Sign out of the current session
post.description:
Revokes the caller's OWN session server-side, so the token they were holding stops
working the moment they sign out rather than lingering until it expires. Idempotent: a
session that is already gone still answers 204, because the caller's intent is met
either way. Open to an enrolment-only session, which must have a way to give up.

401.description: Not authenticated

post.summary: Change an expired password and sign in
post.description:
The self-service path for a user held out of login by a required password change: they
prove identity with their CURRENT password and set a new one, then continue exactly as
Login would have - straight in, or on to the second factor the account owes. Every
other session the account had is revoked, as any password change does. Anonymous
because a held user has no session to authenticate the change with.

requestBody.description: The username, current password, and desired new password

200.description: The password was changed: either a session token, or the same `PasskeyRequired` marker Login returns

400.description: The account does not require a password change, or the new password failed policy

401.description: Invalid credentials, or the account is suspended

429.description: This address has had too many failed sign-in attempts

there is nothing left to test, and it must not remain an anonymous "connect to any host" probe
on a live install. Resolves the connection from the request (decoding the `.ampbus` blob
when present), then attempts a live connection. A supplied CA cert is written to a throwaway file
for the duration of the test only.

Anonymous setup step, but one-way: once `bootstrap.local.json` is written the connection is
sealed (re-running would turn a network outage into an admin-account-creation vector), so this
refuses when already configured. Tests the connection before writing, persists any CA cert,
reloads configuration, and returns the freshly computed setup phase so the boot gate advances.

200.description: The connection was saved; the body carries the fresh setup status

400.description: The request could not be resolved (malformed blob), no server URL was supplied, or a user name or password in an address is not percent-encoded (`auth.setup.database.busUserInfoNotEncoded`)

503.description: The connection could not be established; the body names the cause (`auth.setup.database.bus*`)

its ordinary waiting spinner rather than a ladder.

Clears this machine's connection details and the tunnel it was building, returning the
     wizard to its first step. Anonymous, like every other setup step, and refused once the
     machine has actually joined - at that point it is a member of an installation and this is
     no longer a setup question.

     It exists because the address in a join file is typed by hand at the other end, and a
mistyped one leaves this machine waiting for a caller that is knocking somewhere else
entirely, with nothing here able to fix it.

post.description:
Kicks off managed-NATS provisioning in the background (download is slow) and returns
immediately. The wizard polls Task<IActionResult> AuthController.ProvisionStatus(CancellationToken ct) for Downloading, Configuring,
Testing, done, then reads the join info + fresh phase from the final status.
Anonymous setup step. The same one-way seal as Task<IActionResult> AuthController.SaveDatabase(DatabaseSetupRequest request, CancellationToken ct) refuses once the
connection is configured, with one exception: a provisioning that failed after writing
the connection may be run again, since the wizard's retry is the only way out of it. The
bus starts single-machine; the network step expands it when other machines will join.

forwarded to the agent over NATS as the next arrives from the browser, so the browser experiences
true end-to-end throughput rather than local disk write speed. Unless the caller holds
`files.bypassrestrictions`, a bus-path destination whose name the upload file-type policy
blocks is refused here with the upload's code and audit, before anything is allocated; the
content is judged at commit. When the shard has a disk budget, a declared size that would take
the shard past the point its usage scan stops it at is refused with 409
`files.error.uploadExceedsBudget` (`files.error.uploadExceedsBudgetUnmeasured` when no
scan has measured the shard and the file alone is larger than the budget), counting the latest
scan, uploads committed since it and the shard's other open sessions, less the file the upload
replaces. The response includes `via`
(`agent` or `direct`) so the client can surface the routing.

user, so no per-path check runs here (that happened at upload-start and runs again at upload-commit).

begins forwarding the previous chunk to the agent over NATS while reading this chunk from the HTTP
body, returning only when both are done so the browser gets accurate backpressure from the agent.

as upload-start judges a declared size; the one that would cross it is refused with 409
`files.error.uploadExceedsBudget` and the session is abandoned, its temp file or its partial
destination deleted.

get.description:
The single source of truth polled by the client boot gate.
Auth-independent and anonymous. The reported phase is one of: `setup-database` or
`setup-admin` (the first-run wizard still needs to run), `waiting` (a bus is
configured but currently unreachable), `starting` (settling after boot), or
`ready` (fully operational).

A preview build adds two more, and keeps answering here when it is refusing to answer
anywhere else - this is how the client learns why: `preview-licence` (no valid licence,
so an administrator has to activate one) and `preview-blocked` (expired, running on an
untrustworthy clock, or offline). Such a build also carries a `preview` block on every
status, giving its expiry date, the days left and what it knows about a newer build (whether
one is available, and once expired whether it is installing it, could not, or found none);
a release build carries none.

Every status also says whether THIS request travelled in clear text from a public address
(`plainText`): plain HTTP, and a peer that is neither this machine nor a private
network. The login screen warns on it, as AMP 2 did; a connection from localhost or a LAN
address never sees the warning, and one that arrived over TLS, directly or through a
trusted proxy, does not either.

nothing to act on.

shard restarts into its own spire's versions directory, never this machine's. It deliberately
does NOT compare against the webapi's own version: only the agent project carries Nerdbank
versioning, so that comparison would mark every agent permanently out of date. When the owning
spire is itself behind the installation, `spireBehind` says so, because then a restart
cannot bring the agent up to date and the spire is what needs updating.

goes to the owning spire as a stop and relaunch whenever that spire is online, so the restart
this verdict asks for adopts the newer agent. With the spire offline the restart stays
in-process through the agent, on the same binary, and the verdict stays out of date.

post.summary: Purge an orphan directory from a datastore
post.description:
Permanently deletes a true-orphan directory in a datastore, one with no matching shard,
active or deleted. Directories that belong to a (possibly soft-deleted) shard are refused
here and must go through the shard restore/purge path so their KV records are handled too.
The name must be a single directory leaf with no path separators or traversal. The
resolved path is checked to stay inside the datastore root, and a directory that
matches a known shard's home on this datastore is refused. A directory left behind by
a completed move (the shard now lives elsewhere) is treated as a stale copy and may be
purged. On failure the underlying OS reason is surfaced. The datastore is rescanned
afterwards, and the fresh usage report is returned.

post.description:
Reclaims space by permanently deleting ALL true-orphan directories in one datastore in a
single sweep - the ones with no matching shard, plus stale copies left behind by a completed
move (whose shard now lives on another datastore). A directory that is a known shard's home
on this datastore (active OR soft-deleted) is never touched - those keep their restore/purge
path so their KV records are handled too - and neither is a directory AMP reserves for itself,
such as the one holding every shard's backups. Each delete is path-checked to stay inside the
datastore root; a directory that can't be deleted (locked, permissions) is skipped and the
rest still proceed. The datastore is rescanned afterwards and the fresh usage report returned.

post.summary: Purge shards past their retention window
post.description:
Bulk-purges every shard on this spire that has been soft-deleted for longer than the
retention window (30 days), the housekeeping "Purge old" action. Every bus credential those
shards were launched with is revoked first, here, since only this host can re-sign the bus
account; a shard whose credentials cannot be revoked refuses the whole purge and nothing is
removed. The work then runs on the spire that owns the shards, never on the machine that
received the request, and continues there after this returns: each shard is stopped (in case
an agent lingers), has its KV records removed, and its working directory deleted. The outcome,
including any shard that could not be purged and is left for the next run, is written to the
audit log, and the spire's usage report is refreshed. Irreversible.

since disabling writes and forcing the flush are two separate commands.

quiesceAckRegex.description: Console line proving the flush finished - "Saved the game" and the like.

quiesceSettleDelayMilliseconds.description: After issuing string ApplicationLifecycle.QuiescenceCommand, how long to wait before touching files.

ApplicationLifecycle.description:
Defines how an application launches, is detected as ready, and shuts down:
executable paths, command-line arguments, ready/exit behaviour, and quiescence.

hasWriteableConsole.description: The app accepts commands typed into its console

hasReadableConsole.description: The app produces console output AMP can read

udpLogger.description: The app emits its log over UDP rather than to the console

supportsLiveSettingsChanges.description: The app can apply setting changes at runtime without a restart

liveSettingChangeCommandFormat.description: Console command format used to apply a live setting change: {0}=key, {1}=value

adminMethod.description: The channel used to send admin commands to the app

remoteAdminPassword.description:
Template default for the remote-admin (RCON/telnet) password,
surfaced as the `$RemoteAdminPassword` shared variable. Usually
blank in the template; the per-shard value is generated at creation
and stored in the shard config under the same key.

useRandomAdminPassword.description:
When true, AMP owns the admin password: it is randomly generated and
the user has no say (the safe default for most templates). When
false, the user supplies and manages it. See bool ApplicationManagement.PersistRandomPassword.

persistRandomPassword.description:
Only meaningful with bool ApplicationManagement.UseRandomAdminPassword. When true,
the generated password is kept across starts; when false (default),
a fresh one is generated on every start.

rconConnectDelaySeconds.description: Seconds to wait after the app starts before attempting the first RCON connection

rconHeartbeatMinutes.description: Interval in minutes between RCON heartbeat commands; 0 disables the heartbeat

rconHeartbeatCommand.description: Command sent to keep the RCON connection alive on each heartbeat

ignoreSTDOUTAfterRCON.description:
For games whose STDOUT becomes noise/duplicate once the remote console (RCON)
is live: stop forwarding the process's STDOUT to the console once RCON connects.

rconSelectIPMethod.description: Which local address AMP connects to for RCON

telnetLoginFormat.description: Format for the telnet login/authentication line: {0}=password

telnetNewLineType.description: Line-ending sent on the telnet admin channel

tailLogFilePath.description: Path to the log file tailed when AdminMethods.TailLogFile is in use

applicationIPBinding.description: Template default for the bind address; per-shard override via the $ApplicationIPBinding setting

forceIPBinding.description: The app MUST be given an explicit bind address (never run unbound)

supportsIPv6.description:
The app can bind to an IPv6 address. When false (the default, AMP 2 parity:
e.g. TF2/srcds), an IPv6 bind is rejected at start and IPv6 addresses are not
offered as binding options.

useSteamQueryForStatus.description:
Track connected users by polling the app's Steam query port rather than by reading the
console (AMP 2's App.UseSteamQueryForStatus). For titles that report nothing usable on
STDOUT, this is the only way AMP can tell whether anyone is playing - and therefore the
only way sleep mode can know the server is empty.

maxUsers.description:
Template-declared maximum concurrent users/players; surfaced as the
`$MaxUsers` shared variable. 0 = unlimited (the default).
Per-shard overrides are stored in the shard config under the same key.

environmentVariables.description:
Environment variables set on the app process, on top of the inherited environment.
             Values carry the usual `{{$FullBaseDir}}`-style template tokens, and may reference
             the INHERITED value of a variable as `%NAME%` - which is what makes an append like
             `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` possible rather than a destructive replace:

             ```"LD_LIBRARY_PATH": "{{$FullBaseDir}}linux64:{{$FullRootDir}}linux64:%LD_LIBRARY_PATH%"```Not optional dressing: on Linux this is how a title finds its bundled shared objects and
how loader shims are installed (LD_PRELOAD, BepInEx/doorstop). A title whose
template declares these will fail to start, or start crippled, without them.

ApplicationManagement.description:
How AMP administers a running application: console/RCON access, admin credentials,
IP binding behaviour, and declared user capacity.

ApplicationState.description: The lifecycle state of a shard, from stopped through configuring, running, sleeping, and failure

id.description: Stable unique identifier for this template definition

schemaVersion.description: Version of the AppSpec schema this document conforms to, for forward migration

templateSlug.description:
The template slug as it appears in the repository (e.g. "ark-se", "minecraft").
Derived from the .kvp filename. Stable across updates.

lifecycle.description: How the application launches, becomes ready, and exits

management.description: How AMP administers the running application (console, RCON, IP binding, capacity)

metadata.description: Descriptive and platform metadata (display name, OS/arch support, container policy, release state)

console.description: How AMP reads and interprets the application's console output

portReferences.description: Named port references used to resolve which port serves each role (admin, primary, sleep query)

updateStages.description: Ordered stages that install and update the application (SteamCMD, downloads, extraction, etc.)

preStartStages.description:
Stages run on EVERY start, after PreStart and before the app
launches (App.PreStartStages - same shape as update stages, e.g.
Factorio creating its world save). Condition gating typically
makes them one-time in practice.

portRequirements.description: Network ports the application needs, with their roles, protocols, and ranges

versionSources.description:
Upstream manifests this app's installable versions are read from, so version settings can be
real dropdowns rather than a free-text box. Empty for the majority of templates, whose
download URL is fixed or resolved by an update stage.

settings.description: The configurable settings exposed for this application (command-line args, config-file values, presentation)

configFileMappings.description: How settings are read from and written back to the application's config files

events.description:
Events this application reports on its console, declared as regexes whose named capture
groups become the event's parameters. They appear in the schedule editor's trigger picker
beside AMP's own events and behave identically once fired.

backupExclusions.description:
Files this application produces that are worthless in a backup - logs, crash dumps,
             caches. AMP 2 carried these in a `.backupExclude` file shipped inside the template's
             data; declaring them here instead keeps the whole application definition in one document.

             Used once, to seed a new shard's exclusion list (.amp/.usersnapshotignore) - after
that the list is the user's, and the file manager's snapshot toggle edits it. Paths are
relative to the app's base directory and use the same grammar as that file:
logs/ for a folder and its subtree, *.log for a single-segment glob.

locale.description:
The template's own translations, keyed by language, in Transloco's own shape. Any
user-facing string elsewhere in the spec may be a key into this table.

containerRuntimeAvailable.description:
Whether AMP has a container image it can run this app in. Not authored: the API sets it when
a spec is served, from the live ContainerImageCatalog for whatever
image this template names, and it is false only when that image is one of AMP's own that the
image publisher has not built. A spec read from disk or the bus carries the default, true.

Carried on the spec so the catalogue can grey the app out using the SAME table the
launcher resolves against, rather than the browser keeping its own copy of which images
exist. It is spire-independent on purpose - whether a missing image actually BLOCKS creation
also depends on whether the app would be containerised on the chosen spire, which is the
caller's half of the question (see ContainerModePolicy.CanCreate).

AppSpec.description:
The complete definition of a manageable application (a game server or app),
parsed from a template's .kvp file. Everything AMP needs to install, configure,
launch, monitor, and update a shard of this application.

message.description: A coded reason for the phase (a locale key), when there is one to give

oneOf.description: What a preview build says about itself; null on a release build

plainText.description:
The request that fetched this status came over plain HTTP from a public address, so the
sign-in details about to be typed would travel in clear text. Decided per request by the
status endpoint (PlainTextAccess); the login screen shows
its warning on it. Never set on a status a setup action returns.

AppStatus.description: One status, the single source of truth for "what state is the app in?"

paths.description: Source paths to include, relative to the shard working directory. Folders are included recursively

destination.description: Destination path for the new zip, relative to the shard working directory. The caller owns the .zip extension

ArchiveBody.description: Sources plus a destination for an in-place archive

entries.description: Number of files in the archive (folders are implied by their contents, not counted)

totalSize.description: Total size on disk after extraction, in bytes

ArchiveInfoDto.description: What an archive holds, so the user can be told before unpacking it

id.description: Unique identifier for this audit entry, used as the subject suffix on the stream

tenantId.description: Tenant the event belongs to, scoping it to the tenant's audit stream

timestamp.description: When the action occurred, in UTC

severity.description: How significant this event is for alerting purposes

action.description:
Categorised action identifier, e.g. "ApplicationStarted", "ServerUpdated",
"UserLoggedIn", "TaskCancelled", "ScheduleCreated".
Should be PascalCase and stable across versions - used for filtering/querying.

targetType.description: Entity type the action was performed on, e.g. "Instance", "User"

targetId.description: ID of the entity the action was performed on

taskId.description:
If this event is linked to a ManagedTask, its ID is recorded
here so the audit log can link out to the task queue entry.

oneOf.description:
The thread of the root this event descends from: the user's request, the system's tick or
the schedule's firing that started the flow. Every event of the flow carries it, however many
tasks, bus hops or relaunches lie between. Stamped by `AuditWriter` from the ambient
action; null only on an event written before this existed, which no tree can hold.

The action this event was written inside: the request, the task, the command a spire took
up. Events of one action group under the first of them in the tree. Stamped by
`AuditWriter`; an event without one was written before it was stamped.

The action that caused ActionId? AuditEvent.ActionId, which this event's action hangs under in the
tree. Null when the event was written in a root action: the request, tick or firing itself.
An event of a continued flow (a task reply, a spire's command, a relaunch) always has one, so
a child never reads as a root.

origin.description:
How this event came to be (see AuditOrigin): directly in a request the user
made, inside the flow such a request started, on the system's own initiative, from a
schedule, or under impersonation. Independent of TaskPrincipal AuditEvent.Principal, which says who. An
event written before this existed reads as AuditOrigin.System.

oneOf.description:
Who started the flow this event belongs to: the user behind the click, or the system source
behind the tick. On a root event it is the event's own TaskPrincipal AuditEvent.Principal; on a flow
event it is how the user is named without being made the actor of what the system did.
Null only on an event written before this existed, where TaskPrincipal AuditEvent.Principal stands in.

details.description:
Optional free-form JSON payload for additional context, e.g.
`{"PreviousVersion":"1.0","NewVersion":"1.1"}`. Not queried
directly - present for human/diagnostics inspection.

originIp.description:
Remote IP the triggering request came from, when the event originated
from an HTTP request. Filled automatically by `AuditWriter` from
the ambient HttpContext; null for system/background-originated events.

originSpireId.description:
The spire whose process raised this event - i.e. which AMP node was serving the request.
             Filled automatically by `AuditWriter`, so every event carries it without call sites
             having to remember.

             A multi-node install writes into ONE shared audit stream, so without this an entry says
what happened and to whom but not where, and "which of my front ends is that scanner
actually hitting" has no answer. Null only for events written before this existed.

originNode.description:
The machine name of the node that raised the event. Redundant against
Guid? AuditEvent.OriginSpireId and kept anyway: the id is the durable handle, but it needs a
lookup to mean anything, and an audit entry read during an incident should be legible on
its own - including for a spire that has since been removed.

AuditEvent.description:
An immutable record of a significant action that occurred in the system.
Appended to a JetStream stream - never mutated, never deleted in normal
operation.

Subject pattern: `amp.tn.{tenant}.audit.{auditId}`
Stream filter: `amp.tn.*.audit.>`

actions.description: Each action seen, with how many events carry it

users.description: Each acting user seen, with how many events they produced

targetTypes.description: The distinct target types present in the window

origins.description: Each origin seen, with how many events carry it

AuditFacets.description: Distinct-value counts used to populate the audit log's filter dropdowns

AuditOrigin.description:
How an audit event came to be, as distinct from who it names: PrincipalKind TaskPrincipal.Kind
says WHO acted, this says HOW the action arose. The seam it draws is between "a user did this,
in the request they made" and "the system did this, inside the flow that request started": the
same System principal (an updater, a launcher, a reconciler) carries a different origin depending
on whether a user's click is behind it. Numbered explicitly because the value is stored on the
audit stream; an event written without one reads as AuditOrigin.System.

total.description: Total number of events matching the query across all pages

pageSize.description: Maximum number of events per page

caughtUp.description: True when the in-memory index has finished replaying the stream, so the result is complete rather than partial

items.description: The audit events on this page

AuditQueryResult.description: A page of audit events plus the paging totals the UI needs to render controls

correlationId.description: The flow's thread, which `GET api/audit/tree/{correlationId}` expands

root.description: The root event: the user's request, the system's tick or the schedule's firing, or the flow's first event when the request or tick wrote none of its own. When RootMissing, the earliest event the index holds instead

eventCount.description: Every event of the flow, the root included

maxSeverity.description: The loudest severity any event of the flow carries

rootMissing.description: True when the index dropped events of the flow from its window and none of those it still holds was written by the request or tick itself: the flow is listed on its earliest held event, which may not be its first and is not passed off as the root

AuditRootItem.description: One flow as the roots listing shows it: its root event and the span of what followed

pageSize.description: Maximum number of flows per page

caughtUp.description: True when the index has finished replaying the stream

AuditRootsResult.description: A page of flows, newest root first unless asked otherwise

AuditSeverity.description: How loud this audit event should be treated by alerting/dashboards

rootMissing.description: True when the root event may have been dropped from the index window and the earliest held event stands at the top instead

AuditTree.description: One flow as a tree: the root, then everything that came from it, nested by cause

children.description: The events hanging under it, earliest first

AuditTreeNode.description: One event in a flow's tree, with the events it caused beneath it in time order

passkeysAvailable.description: Whether a passkey ceremony started from this origin would work

passkeyStatus.description: The verdict name, e.g. "IpAddressHost" - see PasskeyOriginStatus

passkeyMessageKey.description: Transloco key explaining the verdict to the user

rpId.description: The relying-party id passkeys are bound to, when one could be derived

expectedOrigin.description: The origin passkeys are bound to, when one could be derived

passkeyPolicy.description:
How hard this installation pushes passkeys - "Optional", "Encouraged" or "Required". Not
sensitive: the sign-in screen reveals it by behaviour anyway, and the enrolment step needs
it before anyone has a token in order to know whether declining is even offered.

AuthCapabilitiesDto.description: What this installation can offer at sign-in, from the caller's current origin

token.description: Signed JWT bearer token to send on subsequent requests

expiration.description: UTC instant at which the token stops being valid

AuthResponse.description: The issued auth token and when it expires, returned to a successful sign-in

productName.description: Product name to display. Blank = the client falls back to "AMP"

loginWelcomeText.description: Free-text welcome shown on the login screen

logoUrl.description: Logo URL. Blank = the client falls back to its bundled emblem

BrandingDto.description: The operator's public-facing branding for the pre-auth screens

servers.description: Bus endpoint URLs the joining machine should connect to

prefix.description: Subject/namespace prefix scoping this install on the bus

hostCandidates.description: Reachable host addresses to try, best-first

caCert.description: PEM CA certificate for a TLS bus; empty when TLS is not used

joinBlob.description: A single encoded `.ampbus` descriptor bundling all of the above for one-paste joining

BusConnectionInfo.description: Everything another machine needs to join this install's message bus

joinInfo.description: Connection details other machines use to join

firewall.description: What the firewall sweep the expand ran did with the bus port's rule

BusExpansion.description: The answer to an expand: the join information to share, and what became of the bus port in the firewall

managed.description: True when AMP itself provisions and supervises the bus (versus an external one)

isPublic.description: True when the bus is already reachable by other machines

oneOf.description: Connection details other machines use to join; present only when public

servers.description: Configured endpoint URLs, populated for an external (unmanaged) bus

BusInfo.description:
State of this install's message bus, for the "add a machine" flow:
    * Managed=false: an external bus - AMP can't reconfigure it; Servers are
            the configured endpoints.
* Managed=true, IsPublic=false: AMP-managed single-machine - can be expanded.
* Managed=true, IsPublic=true: already reachable; JoinInfo is ready to share.

outcome.description: Whether the rule now opens the port, and if not, why not

generation.description: The published state generation that carries the open rule; null unless the outcome is Open

agentRunning.description: Whether the system agent, which applies the published state, was seen running. When it is not, nothing opens the port and it has to be opened by hand

BusPortFirewall.description: The bus port's firewall rule as the expand left it

BusServiceCondition.description: What the panel can tell about the bus service from the record it leaves

condition.description: What the record says, or that there is none

pid.description: nats-server's process id while it runs

startedAtUtc.description: When the running nats-server was launched

binaryVersion.description: The release the running or last server was launched from

configHash.description: SHA-256 of the config the running or last server was launched from

configCurrent.description: Whether that hash matches the config file as it is now; false while a restart the panel asked for is pending

fileStoreBytes.description: The file-store cap the service measured at the last launch

lastExitReason.description: Why the last server is gone, or what the service waits for

serviceVersion.description: The amp3-host build that wrote it

serviceUp.description: A service that is up, whatever it is doing: it acts on a config the panel writes

BusServiceStatus.description: The bus service as the panel sees it, for the wizard, the Support page and the diagnostics bundle

bytes.description: Total size of the files measured

truncated.description: A cap stopped the measurement, so long CandidateSize.Bytes is a floor rather than a total

unreadableDirectories.description: Directories that could not be read, so their contents are not counted

links.description:
Symbolic links found and not followed. An import recreates the ones pointing inside the server
and leaves the rest behind, so a non-zero count is worth telling the user before they import.
Zero when the privileged agent did the measuring, because it does not count them.

isUnderstated.description: Nothing measured here can be trusted as a total

CandidateSize.description: How big a candidate is, and whether we managed to see all of it

CandidateSource.description:
Where a candidate was found, which becomes the source badge on its row. Recorded at scan time
rather than inferred later, because the same directory can be reachable several ways and the
honest answer is "this is how we got here".

scope.description: The scope root the node applies at

dangerous.description: Whether the capability is flagged as dangerous

pathScopable.description: Whether the capability can be narrowed to a path

byNameOnly.description:
Whether the capability is held only through a grant that names it: the superuser grant and
every wildcard over it leave it out, so the role editor shows it as not held under them

CapabilityDto.description: One capability from the permission catalogue

commonEmits.description: Signal names commonly emitted by triggers, offered for condition editing

CatalogDto.description: The trigger and task catalogs plus common emitted signals that drive the schedule editor

currentPassword.description: The current password, used to prove identity since the user has no session

ChangeExpiredPasswordRequest.description: Credentials for the forced/expired password-change flow

currentPassword.description: The caller's existing password, verified before the change

newPassword.description: The replacement password, subject to the configured strength policy

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Request to change the caller's own password

hostName.description: The domain name to look up

CloneContent.description:
What a shard clone copies. CloneContent.Configuration is the shard's SETTINGS - the config
             values, container mode, and start-on-boot held in KV; CloneContent.Data is the on-disk
             working directory (installed game files, world/save data). They compose, so CloneContent.Both
             is a full duplicate.

             Config-only clones need no downtime (pure KV). Any clone that includes CloneContent.Data
requires the SOURCE shard to be stopped, so its files are at rest while they are copied.

newName.description: Display name for the new shard

content.description: What to duplicate: configuration, on-disk data, or both. `None` is rejected

targetSpireId.description: Spire to place the clone on; null clones in place on the source's spire

CompatibilityModes.description: Console-buffering and platform quirks an application needs worked around (combinable flags)

flowId.description: The handle returned by the begin call

rememberMe.description: Issue a long-lived session that survives closing the browser

CompleteRequest.description: The assertion coming back from the browser

Condition.description:
One condition row: a {@Var} template on the left, an operator, and a comparand template on
the right (unused for IsEmpty/IsNotEmpty). String operators compare case-insensitively;
numeric operators parse both sides invariant-culture and yield an explicit condition error
(journaled, treated as non-match) when an operand isn't numeric.

configFile.description: Relative path within the app's base directory

configFileTemplate.description: Optional template file copied/merged when generating string ConfigFileMapping.ConfigFile

configFormat.description: Format string used when writing a value: {0}=key, {1}=value

configFormatRegex.description:
Regex used when reading - named groups 'key' and 'value'. Left at
string ConfigFileMapping.DefaultConfigFormatRegex, lines are read through the inverse of
string ConfigFileMapping.ConfigFormat instead (`ConfigLineSyntax`)

configHeaderFormat.description: Format for a section heading line: {0}=heading

configHeaderRegex.description: Regex used when reading a section heading line - named group 'header'

configEncoding.description: Text encoding: "utf8"/"utf8-nobom" (default), "utf16-le-nobom", or a named encoding

autoMap.description: When true, AMP merges values into an existing/template file in place (import-style)

importable.description: Whether existing values in this file may be imported back into settings

subsections.description: The sections written when generating the file from scratch

ConfigFileMapping.description:
Parsed from {name}metaconfig.json - describes how to read/write each config file
that backs the settings manifest entries. Mirrors AMP 2's `MetaConfigFile`.

path.description: The config file, relative to the shard's file-manager root

content.description:
The edited file to import and then save. Omit it to import the file as it already stands on
disk, which is how a change made outside AMP (over SFTP, or by the app itself) is picked up

ConfigImportRequest.description: A request to read an AMP-managed config file back into the shard's settings

applied.description: Settings whose value the file changed

excluded.description:
Settings present in the file that AMP holds authority over and did not read back (ports and
IP bindings, chiefly). AMP writes its own value over these again on the next start

missing.description:
Settings AMP manages whose key is no longer in the file. AMP only rewrites keys that are
already there, so these have stopped reaching the app

ConfigImportResponse.description: What an import changed. Only names are returned, never values - the file can hold secrets

user.description: Their connection, as the server's user list has it

oneOf.description: Their Steam profile, when they are known by a Steam64 id and it could be looked up
Their Minecraft profile, when they are known by a Mojang UUID and it could be looked up

profileState.description: As string ProfilesAnswer.State, or `none` when they are not known by an id that can be looked up

analyticsKey.description:
The key their analytics are filed under, when the caller may see who users are on this server
and analytics has seen them; the way to their analytics card

oneOf.description: What their address says about who is behind it, when it is known and the caller may see addresses

othersAtAddress.description:
How many other users have connected from their address, when the caller holds
`analytics.addresses` here and the address is one where that means something

userKey.description: Their key, for a reader allowed to see addresses, so the users at their address can leave them out

recoveredAddress.description:
Where they really connected from, when the server saw a relay's address and the connection could
be followed back through AMP's relays with certainty; the kind and the count are then this one's

ConnectedProfile.description: Somebody connected to a server right now, with what is known about them beyond the server's own list

name.description: Display name reported by the application

id.description: Stable application-side user identifier (e.g. UUID, SteamID), when the app provides one

sessionId.description: Identifier for this particular connection, distinguishing repeat connects by the same user

endpoint.description: Remote address the user connected from, when known

idKind.description: What kind of id Id is, which decides where it may be compared (see UserIdKinds)

ConnectedUser.description: A user currently connected to a shard's application (game server, voice server, etc.)

lines.description: The console lines in this page, in ascending sequence order

hasMore.description: True when older history exists before this page's first line

ConsoleHistoryPage.description: A page of console history, oldest-first, plus whether older lines remain to fetch

command.description: The command string to write to the shard's stdin

promptReply.description: True when the command answers an interactive prompt (a Steam password or Guard code), so it is never audited in the clear

ConsoleInputBody.description: Request body carrying a single console command to send to a shard

streamId.description: Identifier of the source stream this line came from

text.description: The line text (English fallback for localised markers)

seq.description: Per-shard monotonic sequence used to merge history with the live feed

kind.description: `line` for ordinary output, `marker` for an inline lifecycle event, `notice` for a notice, `error` for a failure reported on the shard, or `info` for an information line whose Text is its title

state.description: ApplicationState carried by a state marker; null otherwise

success.description: Outcome carried by an update-complete marker; null otherwise

code.description: i18n key for an AMP-authored marker message; null for app output or uncatalogued lines

params.description: Parameters for the localised Code message; null when there are none

level.description: Structured log level parsed from the console format regex; null when unmatched or unconfigured

origin.description: Structured origin/source field parsed from the console format regex; null when unmatched

ConsoleLineDto.description:
One console history entry, ready for the UI. Two kinds:
      • `line`   - ordinary console output from a stream.
      • `marker` - a lifecycle event (start/stop/update) surfaced inline
        so the console visually separates runs. int? ConsoleLineDto.State carries
        the ApplicationState for state markers; bool? ConsoleLineDto.Success the
        outcome for update-complete markers (with State null).
    long ConsoleLineDto.Seq is a per-shard monotonic sequence assigned by the
server-side history buffer - clients use it to merge the REST history
snapshot with the live SignalR feed without duplicates.

filterMatchRegex.description: Regex to strip ANSI escape codes / noise from raw output

filterMatchReplacement.description: Replacement text substituted for each string ConsoleSpec.FilterMatchRegex match

throwawayMessageRegex.description: Lines matching this are discarded entirely before storage

appReadyRegex.description: When this matches, the app is considered Ready

serverAuthURLPromptRegex.description:
Server authentication URL prompt (e.g. Hytale's OAuth device flow): when this
matches a console line, the shard enters AwaitingUserAction and surfaces the URL
the operator must visit. If the regex has a `url` named group, that's the URL;
otherwise the whole match is used.

serverAuthAckRegex.description: Acknowledgement that server authentication completed - clears the prompt

userJoinRegex.description:
Matches a console line announcing a user connecting. Named groups: `username`
(required), `userid`, `sessionid`, and `endpoint` (or `ip`) for the address.

userIdKind.description:
What kind of id the `userid` group captures (see UserIdKinds), which
decides whether one person is recognised across servers. Empty means undeclared: a SteamID is
still recognised by its shape, and anything else is only compared between shards of this
template. Declare it when the id is global, and make it specific (`minecraft-uuid`).

userLeaveRegex.description: Matches a console line announcing a user disconnecting

userChatRegex.description: Matches a chat message line; typically captures the user and message text

preConnectRegex.description:
For games that announce a connecting player across multiple lines.
Fires before ConnectIPRegex; must capture an `id` group that
correlates with either the `id` group in ConnectIPRegex or the
`username`/`userid` in UserJoinRegex. An optional `userid`
group supplies the user's id when the join line has none, matched up by
the name in `id`: Minecraft's "UUID of player Steve is ..." line.

connectIPRegex.description:
Captures the joining player's IP when it does not appear on the same
line as UserJoinRegex.  Must include an `ip` capture group.
Optional `id` group ties this line to a specific player (or
PreConnect entry); without it, the IP is assigned to the most-recently

downloadProgressRegex.description:

a custom downloader). Named capture groups: `percent` (required),
`progressValue` + `progressUnits` and `totalValue` +
`totalUnits` (optional, used to compute transfer speed). When this matches,
the line is consumed as a structured progress event and not published to the
console stream (keeps the transcript clean).

startupProgressRegex.description:
Matches console lines reporting how far through STARTING the application is, for apps whose
             startup is slow but measurable (Minecraft's "Preparing spawn area: 45%", world generation, big
             modded packs). Named capture groups: `PercentageComplete` (required, the percentage), and
             `stage` (optional, what it is doing - shown beside the bar).

             The line is NOT consumed: unlike a download progress bar, which redraws hundreds of times and
would drown the transcript, a startup progress line is part of the server's own startup log and
users expect to see it. Progress is reported live only and never persisted - it is meaningless
the moment the app is up, and writing every tick to KV would be pure amplification.

logRegex.description:

Any group may be omitted if the log format does not provide it.

the regex but not captured - AMP always records its own UTC receive time.

to send back to the app when it matches. The command is template-expanded
(`{{Setting}}`/`{{$PortRef}}`) and then has the match's capture groups
substituted - `{{0}}` = whole match, `{{1}}`… = numbered groups,
`{{name}}` = named groups. A command may carry embedded newlines to send several
commands. (Hytale uses these to drive its `/auth login device` flow.)

file nobody pasted and a firewall eating the setup port all present identically at the end of the
chain - as a connection that does not happen - and each needs something completely different done
about it. Naming the rungs is what lets an operator see WHERE it stopped instead of only that it
did.The rungs are ordered, and each is only meaningful once the one before it is done. The two in the
middle are the ones that earn the whole thing: string EntryNodeSetupProgress.TunnelConnected answers "is the wire
up", and string EntryNodeSetupProgress.BusReachable answers "is anything listening at the other end of it". Those

IReadOnlyList<string> ImportChangeRecord.SettingsMissing deliberately does not count. A config file almost never holds
every key its template manages, so counting it would make this true on essentially every
import and turn the notice into permanent furniture. Those settings simply take AMP's
defaults, which is the normal outcome rather than a change worth flagging. They stay in the

settings and ports are available at all varies by game and is nothing the user did; whether they

different network setup may want the world and the settings and emphatically not the old ports.

MonitoringSettings.description:
Thresholds for the "running hot" resource-usage warnings on the overview. CPU is a plain usage
percentage (warn as it climbs UP). RAM and disk are about HEADROOM REMAINING: warn when what is
still free drops to/below the threshold. Each takes a QUANTITY: a "%" quantity is the free
SHARE of the total (20% = under a fifth free), an absolute one (e.g. "16GB") is a free AMOUNT.

Disk adds a share of the disk to each tier and applies the LESSER of the two: a spire is short
of storage when its free space is below both the floor (string MonitoringSettings.DiskWarning,
string MonitoringSettings.DiskHigh) and that share of the disk (int MonitoringSettings.DiskWarningShare,
int MonitoringSettings.DiskHighShare). The floor caps what a big disk is asked to keep free (16 GB, not
10% of 4 TB) and the share scales it down on a small one (2 GB on a 20 GB disk, not 16 GB). When
the disk's total size is unknown the floor alone applies. A floor typed as a percentage is
already a share, so the smaller of the two shares applies and the larger never fires on its own.

Two tiers per resource: the amber "warning" level and the red "high" level. Because RAM/disk
measure remaining headroom, "high" is the LOWER figure (less left = worse).

shardId.description: The shard this schedule belongs to (v1: schedules are shard-scoped)

steps.description: The behaviour tree executed on each firing

timeout.description:
Maximum wall-clock time allowed for a single execution (all lanes) before it is
considered timed out.

runAsUserId.description:
The identity the schedule ACTS AS: its steps execute under this user's LIVE permissions,
so a schedule can never perform something its author couldn't do directly. Set to the
user on every create AND update (the last editor authors what runs, so editing someone
else's schedule can't be an escalation path). A missing value fails guarded actions closed.

Durable definition of a shard's scheduled behaviour, stored in NATS KV at
`amp.tn.{tenant}.sched.{id}`: a trigger (when) plus a step TREE (what) -
see Step. Executions are separate JobExecution records;
live health is the separate ScheduleStatus key so frequent status

definition.description:
The stored schedule definition. For a caller without `ScheduleWrite`, every parameter listed

oneOf.description: Most recent run status, or null if it has never run

oneOf.description:
Why AMP turned the schedule off, as a coded error the schedules tab translates. It stays off,
and this stays set, until someone who can manage schedules on the server turns it back on.
A step AMP refused and skipped on the latest run, such as a webhook to a destination the owner may not call

refusalAudited.description:
Whether a refused step has been audited since the schedule was last edited. A destination that
is refused on every firing is recorded once, not once per firing.

ScheduleStatus.description:
Last-run health for a schedule, written by the consumer after every run at
`amp.tn.{tenant}.sched.{id}.status`. Separate from the definition so frequent
status writes never race user edits. Drives the trigger list's warning badge -
AMP 2 parity: a failure is visible ON the trigger itself.

password.description: The same password from the first step, re-presented so this call stands on its own

SessionTotals.description: The headline numbers for one period

running.description: The session had not ended when the records were read

SessionWindow.description: The period a query asks about

Whether a setting applies to containerised shards, native ones, or both.

deployed both ways on the same spire, so one spec has to present differently depending on how
this particular shard was actually deployed.

id.description: Stable action identifier the UI dispatches when the action is invoked

category.description: The settings category the action is grouped under

subcategory.description: The subcategory within that category the action ends, or empty when it follows the whole category

SettingsAvailability.description:
What an import of one candidate could recover, and what it could not. Built before anything is
copied, so the results screen can be honest while the user is still deciding rather than
explaining afterwards.

specs.description: Per-node metadata (input type, category, i18n keys, order) the UI renders each control from

secretHasValue.description: For secret nodes, whether a value is stored (the value itself is never sent)

actions.description: The inline actions available across the settings sections

unavailable.description:
Nodes this machine cannot take a value for, each with the locale key that says why: a node this
build holds at a fixed value (PlatformSettingsLocks), or one the machine's role
rules out. The UI shows such a node read-only with that sentence, and a write to it is refused.

SettingsManifest.description:
The full settings manifest the UI renders from: specs (metadata), current
values keyed by node id, which secret nodes have a stored value, and the
available inline actions. DisplayName/Description/EnumValues in the specs
are TRANSLOCO KEYS - the frontend translates before rendering.

fieldName.description: The setting's identifier, used as its config/command-line key unless string SettingSpec.ParamFieldName overrides it

paramFieldName.description: Optional alternate key to emit on disk / on the command line instead of string SettingSpec.FieldName

effectiveKey.description:
The setting's on-disk / on-command-line key: string SettingSpec.ParamFieldName
when set, otherwise string SettingSpec.FieldName. The single definition used by
config-file generation, template substitution, and command-line building so
the key never derives differently across them.

required.description: The user must provide a value for this setting

hidden.description: The setting is not shown in the UI (still applied from its default/stored value)

platform.description: Host platforms this setting applies to; mirrors a stage's UpdateSourcePlatform

deployment.description: Whether this setting applies to containerised shards, native ones, or both

conditionSetting.description: Setting key that gates this one; shown only when its value matches string SettingSpec.ConditionValue. Mirrors a stage's UpdateSourceConditionSetting

conditionValue.description: Value that string SettingSpec.ConditionSetting must equal for this setting to be shown

defaultValue.description:
Value used when the user has not set one. Null when the template declares none, which is
distinct from an empty default: a setting with no default and no value is left out of a
generated config file, so the application applies its own default.

meta.description: Free-form metadata carried through from the manifest

category.description: Top-level grouping used to organise the settings UI

special.description: Special handling marker (e.g. "array:text", "array:number", "listfile", "fileexists") that changes how the value is written

displayName.description: Label shown for this setting in the UI

description.description: Help text explaining what the setting does

keywords.description: Extra search terms that help users find this setting

inputType.description: The input control to render (e.g. text, number, checkbox, enum)

isSecret.description:
The value is a secret (token, API key, connection string, ...). Secret values are masked
on read and never returned to the client in the clear, independent of string SettingSpec.InputType.
A `password` input is treated as secret automatically; set this for secret-bearing
settings that render as plain text.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text shown in an empty input field

suffix.description: Unit or suffix shown after the input (e.g. "MB", "seconds")

Id of the VersionSource this setting's options come from, for a value list
             that is read from an upstream manifest rather than fixed in the template.

             The list is NOT delivered with the settings payload: the client asks for it when the
control is actually opened. A page carrying a dozen version pickers would otherwise fan out
a dozen upstream fetches nobody asked for. So a setting with this set arrives with its
current value and this id, and nothing else.

minValue.description: Minimum allowed numeric value; null means no lower bound

maxValue.description: Maximum allowed numeric value; null means no upper bound. See bool SettingSpec.IsHostCap

isHostCap.description:
True when MaxValue was imposed by the host's infra cap (e.g. MaxUsersCap), not by the
application manifest. The UI uses this to show "Capped at X by the host" vs. a plain
valid-range hint when the manifest just declares the setting's natural bounds.

NOT IMPLEMENTED - parsed from the manifest and currently read by nothing.
In AMP 2 this scales the STORED value on its way OUT to the config file / command line
(store minutes, emit milliseconds); the UI never sees it. Implementing it means applying
it in `ctx.ResolveFieldValue` AND inverting it in `ConfigFileImporter` - it is
the one attribute that makes the write path non-idempotent, so without the divide, every
import of a merged config file would inflate the value by the multiplier again.

multipleOf.description:
The value should be a multiple of this number. Currently only drives the number input's
`step` attribute in the UI - AMP 2 additionally rounds to the nearest multiple when
writing, and uses whether this is an integer or a float to decide the JSON node's type.

(login URL, Steam Guard request) the UI classifies into a broad reason.

User-configured values. Only contains settings that have been explicitly

User-supplied setting values for a DeployedShard.

apply time (matching AMP2 behaviour).

How AMP should manage the container runtime for this shard.
Always explicitly configured - there is no automatic mode.
The template's ContainerSupport policy surfaces
as a recommendation or requirement hint in the UI only.

usable.description: The credentials the caller may point the shard at: their own and the tenant's Public ones

The shard's configured disk budget in MB at scan time, copied here so a reader of the
report can judge long ShardDiskUsage.SizeMb without fetching every shard's infra settings.

Where long ShardDiskUsage.SizeMb stood against long ShardDiskUsage.LimitMb when this scan ran.
Evaluated on the spire that owns the files, at the moment they were measured, so every
reader - UI banner, start guard, enforcement - agrees on one verdict instead of each
recomputing it from numbers of differing freshness.

ShardDiskUsage.description:
Disk usage of one directory inside a datastore. DiskUsageKind ShardDiskUsage.Kind says which case it is:
  • Active shard - DiskUsageKind.Shard, bool ShardDiskUsage.Deleted false.
  • Soft-deleted shard - DiskUsageKind.Shard, bool ShardDiskUsage.Deleted true
    (the operator can Restore it or Delete it permanently).
  • Orphan - DiskUsageKind.Orphan: data with no matching shard at all
    (surface it, never silently omit).
  • Backups - DiskUsageKind.Backups: every shard's snapshot archives.

False when the operator marked the port not publicly accessible, which suppresses its public
address entirely - showing one would contradict the switch they set.

A shard port together with every address it can be reached on. One per port that is worth
connecting to: the application's primary port always, plus anything the operator has deliberately
published.

reach.description: Whether this is the outside-world address or the same-network one

port.description: Port to dial; meaningless when ShowPort is false

showPort.description:
False only when the operator advertised a bare host and said it carries no port (a reverse proxy
or an SRV record routes it), in which case appending one would send people to the wrong place.

display.description: The address as it should be shown and copied ("host:port", or just "host")

uri.description:
The template's `EndpointURIFormat` applied to this address (e.g. `steam://connect/1.2.3.4:27015`),
or null when the template declares none or the format resolved to something unsafe to hand a browser.

notes.description: What stands between this address and a working connection; empty when nothing does

viaSpireId.description: The front spire serving this address, when it is not the shard's own machine

viaSpireName.description: That front spire's display name, so the UI can name it without a second lookup

How the route carrying this address is doing, or null when nothing is carrying it - a shard
reached on its own machine has no route to have an opinion about. Deliberately separate from the
notes: a note is something to read, this is a fact worth one glyph, and it changes on its own
while somebody is looking at the screen.

ShardEndpointAddress.description:
One resolved way to reach a shard's port, with everything the UI needs to present it honestly:
the address itself, where it came from, and what is known to be in the way.

address.description: The address allocated to the shard on its tunnel, once there is one

ShardGatewayBindingStatus.description:
Live gateway-binding state, written by the front spire's reconciler under a separate KV key (frequent
status writes never race the declaration).

spireName.description: Display name of the spire this shard runs on

spireIsLinux.description: True when the shard's spire runs Linux (drives the container option list)

containerPolicy.description: Numeric ContainerSupport flags from the template's ContainerPolicy

logicalCores.description: Logical CPU count on the spire (caps the CPU-limit slider)

templateOs.description:
Numeric HostPlatform flags from the template's declared OS support. Used by the UI to enforce mandatory
containerisation when the template is Linux-only but the spire runs Windows (Windows=1, Linux=2).

supportsSleep.description:
Whether this application's template declares that it can be put to sleep. False hides the sleep
setting entirely rather than offering a switch that could never do anything - whether an app is
safe to sleep depends on how its clients behave, which only the template maintainer knows.

tracksUsers.description:
Whether this application reports users connecting at all. Analytics and geo filtering both
start from that, so without it their settings can do nothing, and the page says so.

reportsAddresses.description:
Whether it also reports the address a user connected from, which geo filtering and the
country breakdown need.

ShardInfraContext.description:
Infra settings bundled with the spire/template context the UI needs to
render container-mode options and resource-limit controls correctly.

containerImageOverride.description: The image to run instead of the template's; an empty string returns to the template's

extraEnvironment.description: The whole set of extra environment variables, replacing the stored set when present

ShardInfraPatch.description:
A change to a shard's ShardInfraSettings: every field is optional, and one that is
absent or null keeps its stored value.

oneOf.description:
Why the stored `$MaxUsers` was not lowered to a new `MaxUsersCap`, or null when it was
lowered or did not need to be. The cap itself is saved either way.

startOnBoot.description:
Start this shard when the system its spire runs on starts, whether or not it was running
when that system went down. Read once per boot by the owning spire; a restart of AMP alone
starts nothing.

autoRestartOnCrash.description:
If the application reaches the Ready state and then exits unexpectedly
(no stop was requested) after running for at least 5 minutes, the agent
will automatically restart it instead of stopping. Disable to opt out
of this behaviour for shards that intentionally exit after finishing a task.

startupOrder.description:
Determines the order in which shards start on boot.
Lower numbers start first, one shard at a time; shards with the same
order start by name. Default 100; use lower values for dependencies.

sleepMode.description:
Let this shard sleep while nobody is connected: AMP stops it, holds its ports so it still
             appears online, and starts it again the moment someone tries to connect.

             The operator's ONLY say in sleep mode, and the only part of it that belongs to them. Every
timing - how long empty before sleeping, how long to doze, how slow a start disqualifies it -
is a property of how the application's clients behave, so it is set by the template maintainer
on ApplicationLifecycle. This switch does nothing at all unless
that template declares SupportsUniversalSleep, and the UI hides it entirely when it
does not.

advertisedAddress.description:
The address to give people for this shard, overriding everything AMP works out for itself.
             A hostname or IP ("play.example.com"), or one with a port pinned ("play.example.com:25565").
             Empty = AMP resolves it (see `ShardEndpointResolver`).

             It exists because the operator routinely knows something AMP cannot observe: a domain pointed
at the machine, a proxy or SRV record in front of it, a load balancer. Declaring one IS them
saying they have arranged for it to work, so it is reported as given rather than second-guessed.

advertisedAddressIncludesPort.description:
Whether a bare string ShardInfraSettings.AdvertisedAddress still carries the shard's port. False when
something in front routes it - an SRV record or a reverse proxy - and players connect to the
host alone; appending a port then would send them somewhere nothing is listening.
Ignored when the advertised value already pins a port of its own.

containerMode.description: Per-shard container mode - always explicitly set

containerImageOverride.description:
Override the container image specified by the template.
Null = use the template default.

memoryLimitMb.description: Memory limit in MiB. 0 = unlimited (host default)

memoryReservationMb.description:
Memory reservation (soft limit) in MiB. Must be <= MemoryLimitMb when both non-zero.
0 = no reservation.

cpuLimit.description: CPU limit as a fractional number of cores. 0.0 = unlimited

maxUsersCap.description:
Hard ceiling on concurrent players, enforced by AMP regardless of the
application's own `$MaxUsers` setting. 0 = no infra-level cap (the
app setting or template default governs). Intended for slot-based hosting
where the operator sells a fixed number of player slots and must prevent

enableAnalytics.description:
"Enable Analytics": collect data about users who join the server (where available).

             AMP 2's wording, and AMP 2's meaning: with this off the agent records nothing at all, and the
shard contributes no sessions to analytics.

userSpecificData.description:
"Store user-specific data": if enabled, you will be able to see which users spend the most
             time on the server and other data related to specific users. However this requires that you
             disclose the use of analytics to all users who join the server.

             This is the personal-data switch, so in AMP 3 it also governs addresses: with it off the agent
does not look a user's IP up at all, and every session is recorded with an unknown country.

already recorded stay as they were.

minimumSessionTimeForRetention.description:

retained in the analytics data. This can be used to filter out very short sessions that may
not be meaningful for analysis.

enableGeoFiltering.description:
"Enable Geo-Filtering": block connections from certain countries.

             Works the way AMP 2's did: when a user connects from a country this shard does not accept, the
agent sends string ShardInfraSettings.GeoFilterKickCommand to the application's console. Cruder than a
firewall, and better for it: it needs no privilege, works the same on every platform and inside
a container, and the game itself tells the user why. It does need the application to log
connections with an address and to accept a kick command.

blockedCountries.description: "Blocked Countries": countries to block connections from, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.

allowedCountries.description:
"Allowed Countries": countries to allow connections from, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. An empty
list implies that all countries are allowed except those in the block list.

blockUnknownCountries.description:
Also block users whose country cannot be worked out. That includes everybody who arrives through
a published port without gateway mode, because the address the game sees is the tunnel's.

geoFilterKickMessage.description:
"Filtering Message": the message to display to users who are disconnected by geo filtering.
{CountryCode} and {CountryName} are replaced with the user's country.

geoFilterKickCommand.description:
"Kick Command": the console command that disconnects a filtered user. {UserName}, {UserID},
{Reason}, {CountryCode} and {CountryName} are replaced; {Reason} is the filtering message.

diskLimitMb.description:
Disk budget for this shard's working directory in MB. 0 = no limit.

             Deliberately NOT in the resource-limits block above: those are container knobs handed to
Docker/Podman and mean nothing to a native shard, whereas this is measured and enforced by
AMP itself from the spire's periodic usage scan, so it works the same either way.Soft by design. AMP warns as the shard approaches the budget and stops it once it is
meaningfully over (see DiskLimitPolicy); it never gives the application
a full filesystem, because a failed write mid-save is how game servers lose worlds.
The trade is that a shard can exceed this between scans - the budget is what AMP acts on,
not a wall the application can feel.

importConfigFilesFromSftp.description:
When a managed, importable configuration file is written over SFTP, read the change back
             into this shard's settings instead of leaving it to be overwritten on the next start.

             On is the useful default: bulk-editing config is most of what SFTP is for, and without
this a write appears to succeed and is then silently lost the next time AMP regenerates
the file. Off suits a shard whose files are being moved around wholesale - restoring a
backup, syncing a config tree in from elsewhere - where parsing every arriving file back
into settings is not what was meant.Per SHARD rather than per spire because it follows the application, not the machine:
whether a given server's config should be read back depends on its template and how its
owner works with it, and one spire hosts servers that differ.

ShardInfraSaveResult.description:

startOnBoot.description:
Start this shard when the system its spire runs on starts, whether or not it was running
when that system went down. Read once per boot by the owning spire; a restart of AMP alone
starts nothing.

autoRestartOnCrash.description:
If the application reaches the Ready state and then exits unexpectedly
(no stop was requested) after running for at least 5 minutes, the agent
will automatically restart it instead of stopping. Disable to opt out
of this behaviour for shards that intentionally exit after finishing a task.

startupOrder.description:
Determines the order in which shards start on boot.
Lower numbers start first, one shard at a time; shards with the same
order start by name. Default 100; use lower values for dependencies.

sleepMode.description:
Let this shard sleep while nobody is connected: AMP stops it, holds its ports so it still
             appears online, and starts it again the moment someone tries to connect.

             The operator's ONLY say in sleep mode, and the only part of it that belongs to them. Every
timing - how long empty before sleeping, how long to doze, how slow a start disqualifies it -
is a property of how the application's clients behave, so it is set by the template maintainer
on ApplicationLifecycle. This switch does nothing at all unless
that template declares SupportsUniversalSleep, and the UI hides it entirely when it
does not.

advertisedAddress.description:

             A hostname or IP ("play.example.com"), or one with a port pinned ("play.example.com:25565").
             Empty = AMP resolves it (see `ShardEndpointResolver`).

             It exists because the operator routinely knows something AMP cannot observe: a domain pointed
at the machine, a proxy or SRV record in front of it, a load balancer. Declaring one IS them
saying they have arranged for it to work, so it is reported as given rather than second-guessed.

advertisedAddressIncludesPort.description:
Whether a bare string ShardInfraSettings.AdvertisedAddress still carries the shard's port. False when
something in front routes it - an SRV record or a reverse proxy - and players connect to the
host alone; appending a port then would send them somewhere nothing is listening.
Ignored when the advertised value already pins a port of its own.

containerMode.description: Per-shard container mode - always explicitly set

containerImageOverride.description:
Override the container image specified by the template.
Null = use the template default.

memoryLimitMb.description: Memory limit in MiB. 0 = unlimited (host default)

memoryReservationMb.description:
Memory reservation (soft limit) in MiB. Must be <= MemoryLimitMb when both non-zero.
0 = no reservation.

cpuLimit.description: CPU limit as a fractional number of cores. 0.0 = unlimited

maxUsersCap.description:

application's own `$MaxUsers` setting. 0 = no infra-level cap (the
app setting or template default governs). Intended for slot-based hosting
where the operator sells a fixed number of player slots and must prevent
the tenant from raising the in-game limit above what was purchased.
