ShardInfraSettings.description:
Infrastructure and lifecycle settings for a DeployedShard.
These settings belong to AMP, not to the hosted application - they control
how and when the shard runs rather than what it does.

Separated from ShardConfig (application settings) so the two
concerns have distinct ownership, audit trails, and access-control surfaces.

KV key: `amp.tn.{tenant}.sr.{shardId}.infra`

agentVersion.description:
The reporting agent's own build version (Nerdbank.GitVersioning stamp). A metrics sample is
a liveness heartbeat, so carrying the version here keeps string? ShardState.AgentVersion
fresh for a long-running shard that emits no further lifecycle events after its handshake.

cpuPercent.description: Process-tree CPU usage in percent of one core ×100 (0–100 per host normalisation)

memoryMb.description: Resident memory of the application process tree, MiB

memoryLimitMb.description: Configured memory ceiling (0 = unlimited) so charts can show headroom

ioReadKbps.description: Disk read throughput since the previous sample, KiB/s

ioWriteKbps.description: Disk write throughput since the previous sample, KiB/s

activeUsers.description: Connected users/players, from console join/leave tracking (-1 = unknown)

custom.description:
App-defined metrics extracted from console output via the template's
`Console.MetricsRegex` - every named capture group whose value
parses as a number lands here under the group's name (e.g. TPS, MSPT).

listeningPorts.description:
Of the shard's ASSIGNED ports, the ones currently observed listening
(host listener table, protocol-aware). Drives the per-port open/closed
indicators - AMP 2's port summary equivalent.

ShardMetricsSample.description:
One metrics sample published by a shard agent on
`amp.tn.{t}.sr.{id}.ev.metrics` (write-only for the agent, like
lifecycle events). The webapi bridges samples to SignalR for live charts
and keeps a short in-memory history for the detail view; durable long-term
retention can later be layered on via a JetStream stream on the same subject.

assignments.description:
Maps each string PortRequirement.Ref to its assigned base port.
For requirements with int PortRequirement.Range > 1, this is
the lowest port in the range - consecutive ports are implied.
USER-DEFINED custom ports live here too (described by IReadOnlyList<CustomPortDef> ShardPortAssignments.CustomPorts),
so conflict checks, occupied-set collection, renumbering, and port publishing
all treat them exactly like template ports.

customPorts.description:
Metadata for ports the USER registered beyond the app spec (e.g. a Dynmap web port).
Their numbers sit in IReadOnlyDictionary<string, int> ShardPortAssignments.Assignments under string CustomPortDef.Ref.
Unlike template ports these can be deleted again.

privatePortRefs.description:
Refs marked NOT publicly accessible: excluded from port publishing and not opened in the
system firewall. Absence = public. The template's primary application port is public even
when listed here; bool ShardPortAssignments.IsPublic(string portRef, string? primaryRef) is the one answer.

ShardPortAssignments.description:
The concrete port assignments for a DeployedShard.
Each entry maps a string PortRequirement.Ref to the actual assigned
port number. Written once at creation and updated only when ports are
explicitly reassigned.

Kept separate from ShardConfig (user setting values) because
ports are assigned by the system and have different ownership semantics.

KV key: `amp.tn.{tenant}.sr.{shardId}.ports`

ref.description: Stable port reference key (from the template, or the custom port's ref)

name.description: Human-readable port name, falling back to the ref when the template omits one

description.description: Template description of the port's purpose; empty for custom or metadata-less ports

protocol.description: Transport protocol as a string (for example TCP, UDP, or Both)

port.description: The port number currently assigned by the allocator

isPublic.description: True when the port is marked publicly accessible

custom.description: True when this is a user-registered custom port (deletable), false for a template-declared port

ShardPortInfo.description: One declared or custom port for a shard, joining template metadata to its allocated number

available.description: Whether sleep can be used for the current run

reason.description: Why not, in English, when Available is false

reportedAt.description: When the agent last settled the question

ShardSleepStatus.description:
The live operational state of a DeployedShard.
Written frequently by the shard agent - kept in a separate KV key so
high-frequency heartbeat writes don't collide with the durable definition.

KV key: `amp.tn.{tenant}.sr.{shardId}.state`

parentId.description: The snapshot this one derives from; null = a root (full, no ancestor)

name.description: Short operator-facing name, e.g. "Pre-1.20 upgrade"

description.description: Longer free-text description of what this snapshot is / why it was taken

sticky.description: When true, automatic pruning/retention must never delete this snapshot

failureReason.description: Visible reason when SnapshotStatus ShardSnapshot.Status is SnapshotStatus.Failed

skippedFiles.description:
Files the capture could not read, so this snapshot does not contain them. A snapshot with
any of these is still Complete - it is a real backup of everything else - but it is NOT a
complete picture of the disk, and restoring it will not put these files back.

skippedCount.description: How many files were skipped in total (see IReadOnlyList<SkippedFile> ShardSnapshot.SkippedFiles)

archiveMissing.description:
The zip this node names is not where it should be, so the snapshot cannot be restored or
             downloaded even though the timeline still knows about it. The usual cause is a cross-spire
             move that left the backups behind: the graph lives in shared KV and travels with the shard,
             the archives sit on a disk belonging to the spire it came from.

             Stamped by the owning spire when it reads the graph, and cleared again by the same check if
the file reappears. A spire that does not own the shard cannot see its disk and leaves the
flag exactly as it found it, rather than declaring someone else's backups missing.

sizeMb.description: Actual on-disk size of this node's zip, MB (compressed)

uncompressedMb.description: Uncompressed size of this node's captured contents, MB (the 0-compression estimate)

fileCount.description: Number of file entries this node contributes (changed/added for a partial)

ownerSpireId.description:
The spire+run that is capturing this node; a Running node from a different run of
            its owner is a crash leftover, failed on read. Another spire's node is never touched

processedFiles.description: Files processed so far in the SnapshotStage.Processing phase

totalFiles.description: Total files to process this phase (0 = unknown/indeterminate)

datastoreId.description: Datastore the zip is stored in (the `Backups`-tagged one, or the primary)

zipFileName.description: Zip filename relative to the shard's backup root, i.e. `{Id}.zip`

ShardSnapshot.description:
One node in a shard's snapshot timeline (a DAG). Guid? ShardSnapshot.ParentId links to
the snapshot this one derives from; a null parent is a root. Restoring an older
node and snapshotting again forks a new branch off it - which is what produces
the GitHub-style timeline with diverging lanes.

nodes.description: Every snapshot node in this shard's timeline (the DAG)

headId.description: The node whose state is currently laid down on disk; null before the first snapshot

restoringId.description: The node currently being restored onto disk; null when no restore is running

restoreOwnerSpireId.description: The spire+run driving the current restore (for the same stale-reconciliation as capture)

ShardSnapshotGraph.description:
The complete snapshot timeline for one shard: every node, the current
Guid? ShardSnapshotGraph.HeadId ("what's on disk now"), and the per-shard settings.
Stored as a single KV record (`Ns.ShardSnapshots`) so timeline edits are
atomic - mirrors the one-record-per-shard pattern of the usage report.

maxBackupSizeMb.description: Maximum uncompressed size of a single snapshot, MB. 0 = no limit

maxTotalStorageMb.description: Maximum aggregate snapshot storage for this shard, MB. 0 = no limit

stopWhenNoQuiesce.description:
When the app declares no quiescence command, stop the shard for the duration of
the snapshot (consistent capture) rather than snapshotting it hot. Default true.

ShardSnapshotSettings.description: Per-shard guardrails for snapshot storage. Both limits are evaluated pre-flight against the uncompressed (0-compression) size estimate so a snapshot is refused with a visible reason before any zipping work happens. 0 = no limit. Cadence/retention ("cycling") is deliberately out of scope until the scheduler.

revision.description:
The KV revision this copy of the record was read at, which orders any two copies a reader
holds: a copy with a lower revision is older. Set by the reads that reach a browser (the
state feed's push, the REST state read) from the entry they read. Only the entry's revision
counts: a value left inside the JSON by an earlier read that was written back is meaningless,
and no writer of the record reads it.

oneOf.description: Current runtime metrics. Null when the shard is stopped

activeTaskId.description: If a ManagedTask is currently running against this shard, its ID

processId.description: OS process ID of the running application. Null when stopped

runningVersion.description: Version reported by the running process, if available

agentVersion.description:
Build version of the shard AGENT supervising this shard (distinct from
string? ShardState.RunningVersion, which is the hosted app's version). Persisted from the agent's
handshake/heartbeat so the spire knows which agent binary each live shard runs on - the
input to stale-agent restart escalation and version GC. Null until an agent reports in.

lastErrorMessage.description: Set when the shard transitions to a failed state (English fallback)

lastErrorCode.description: Optional i18n key for string? ShardState.LastErrorMessage so the client can localise it

statusMessage.description:
What the agent is doing WITHIN its current state, when it said. A state on its own is often too
coarse to be reassuring: "Pre-Start" for a minute reads as hung, where "Connecting to the
gateway spire" reads as working. Cleared by the next transition that carries no message, so it
can never linger and describe something that finished. English fallback, like
string? ShardState.LastErrorMessage.

statusCode.description: Optional i18n key for string? ShardState.StatusMessage so the client can localise it

startedAt.description:
When the application was last launched, from the agent's most recent Starting transition.
Kept after the shard stops; null only for a shard that has never been started.

oneOf.description:
Whether sleep mode can actually be used right now, and when it cannot, why. Null until the
agent has settled the question (or when the app does not support sleep at all, in which case
the UI hides the whole feature and never consults this).

awaitsLicence.description:
Waiting for a person to accept the application's licence before a start that no person was
waiting on can go ahead. The shard is in the same AwaitingUserAction state an agent's own prompt
puts it in, but no agent runs: the start was refused before anything was launched.

acceptsTraffic.description:
Whether anything on the far side will answer a connection, which is not the same question as
             whether the application is running.

             A sleeping shard has no application process at all, and yet its port must stay reachable: the
whole point of sleep is that the agent holds the port, answers queries on the application's
behalf and starts it again when somebody actually connects. Cutting off a sleeping shard's
traffic removes the only thing that could ever wake it.

SharedCredentialKind.description: What a shared credential signs in to. Open: a kind is added when a consumer exists for it

SharedCredentialView.description:
A credential as a viewer may see it. string? SharedCredentialView.Username is set for the creator alone and
int? SharedCredentialView.ShardCount for the creator and a manager; there is no secret here or anywhere.

SkippedFile.description:
A file a capture could not read and therefore left out of the archive, with the reason the
filesystem gave. Recorded on the snapshot so "what is NOT in this backup" is answerable
without going to the logs - the usual cause being a file the running application holds open
in a way that forbids reading it at all.

SleepWakeupModes.description: Which events can wake a sleeping shard back up (combinable flags)

SnapshotContent.description:
What a snapshot captures - any combination of the three. The split mirrors how
an install is layered: base data is re-downloadable, game state is what the
server generates on top, and AMP config is the management-side settings.

SnapshotKind.description: Whether a snapshot is self-contained or a delta against its parent chain

SnapshotStage.description:
Coarse phase of an in-flight capture/restore, mirroring the update flow's
"gather then process" shape. Gathering is indeterminate (walking the tree,
diffing against the parent); Processing has a real files-done/total percentage.

headSha.description: The source's HEAD commit sha after the sync

changed.description: True when HEAD moved since the previous sync

error.description: A failure message when the sync did not complete, otherwise null

updated.description: When this template definition was last updated (UTC)

aarchSupport.description: Whether the application runs on aarch64 hosts

author.description: Author or maintainer of the template

url.description: Reference URL for the template or application

displayImageSource.description: Icon/image reference for the application (e.g. an internal: id or a URL)

endpointURIFormat.description: Format string for a client connect URI: {0}=endpoint address

configManifest.description: Filename of the settings config manifest

metaConfigManifest.description: Filename of the meta-config manifest describing config-file read/write; empty if none

configRoot.description: Filename of the root .kvp definition this template is built from

specificDockerImage.description: A specific Docker image to run the app in; empty uses the default base image

dockerRequired.description: The app must run inside a container

dockerBaseReadOnly.description: Mount the container's base image read-only

containerPolicyReason.description: Explanation shown alongside ContainerSupport SpecMetadata.ContainerPolicy when it constrains the user's choice

extraSetupStepsURI.description: URL to extra manual setup instructions the app requires

prerequisites.description: Prerequisite packages/components that must be present on the host

extraContainerPackages.description: Additional OS packages to install into the container image

eulaLocation.description:
URL of the end-user licence a user must accept before this app will start, shown by the
             acceptance dialog alongside the setting marked `Special=EULA`.

             Presented as a link that opens in a new tab, never embedded: the licences that matter here
(Minecraft's EULA, the Steam Subscriber Agreement) all refuse to be framed, and a licence
the user cannot actually read is worse than no dialog at all.

releaseNotes.description: Release notes for this template version

breakingReleaseNotes.description: Notes about breaking changes in this template version

deprecatedReason.description: If set, marks the template deprecated and explains why

minAMPVersion.description: Minimum AMP version required to use this template

minAgentVersion.description:
Minimum shard-agent version (semver) required to run this template. Checked at deploy
and at start against the version the spire would launch; a spire whose newest staged
agent is below this refuses with a clear error. Null/empty means no floor.

Distinct from string SpecMetadata.MinAMPVersion: that gates template compatibility with
the AMP install as a whole, this gates the specific agent binary that supervises the
app process (a template may need a newer agent for a capability the old agent lacks).

appIsMultiIPAware.description: The app understands binding to a specific address on multi-IP hosts

SpecMetadata.description:
Descriptive and platform metadata for a template: display info, authorship, supported
OS/architecture, container policy, prerequisites, and versioning/release details.

name.description: Its display name

version.description: The AMP version it reports, or null if unknown

online.description: Whether it can be told to update right now

rolledBackFrom.description: The newer version that spire tried and rolled back, as its heartbeat reports, or null when it reports none

rolledBackKind.description: Why that spire rolled back, as the marker's kind, or null when unknown

SpireBehindDto.description: A spire that did not follow the last update

datastores.description: The datastores this spire offers for shard placement

usageScanIntervalMinutes.description:
How often this spire re-measures its datastores, in minutes.

             Per spire because the right answer is a property of the machine's disks and how much is on
them: a scan walks every file under every datastore, which is nothing on an NVMe holding
four servers and minutes of thrashing on a spinning bulk store holding two hundred. It is
also the resolution of everything built on the scan - a disk limit is noticed, at worst,
one interval after it is crossed - so the operator is choosing directly between how current
those numbers are and what measuring them costs.

resolvedUsageScanInterval.description:
int SpireConfig.UsageScanIntervalMinutes as a usable interval, clamped to the supported range.
        Always read the cadence through this: an out-of-range value in KV (hand-edited, or written
        by an older build) must land on a sane cadence, never on a zero-delay scan loop.

SpireConfig.description:
Operator-controlled configuration for a spire - most importantly the set of
datastores (on-disk locations) it offers for shard placement.

Kept separate from SpireDefinition (identity/heartbeat) because
it is edited by operators and read by the launch path, with different
ownership and write cadence.

KV key: `amp.tn.{tenant}.sp.{spireId}.cfg`

id.description: Stable identifier a deployed shard references to record which datastore it was placed in

name.description: Operator-facing name, e.g. "Fast NVMe", "Bulk HDD"

path.description: Absolute path on the spire host under which shard directories are created

isDefault.description: The datastore used when a shard does not specify one

enabled.description: When false, the datastore is hidden from new deployments

softLimitMb.description:
Soft usage limit in MB. Once the scanned usage reaches this, new shards
cannot be created in this datastore (existing shards keep running and
may still grow - it is a placement guardrail, not a quota). 0 = no limit.

tags.description:
Operator/auto-applied labels for placement and presentation - e.g. the
storage medium ("NVMe", "SSD", "HDD", auto-detected where possible) plus
any free-form tags ("scratch", "backups", "fast").

SpireDatastore.description:
A named on-disk location a spire can place shard working directories in.
Each deployed shard is assigned to one datastore and gets its own
subdirectory beneath string SpireDatastore.Path, which becomes the working directory
of its agent when launched.

id.description: Stable unique identifier for this spire, used throughout the KV hierarchy and NATS subjects

tenantId.description: The tenant that owns this spire

description.description: Optional operator description of what this spire is for

isLocal.description:
The machine AMP itself runs on. Exactly one auto-seeded local spire exists
per tenant; it cannot be deleted.

platform.description: The OS this spire runs on - determines which executables and paths apply

architecture.description: The CPU architecture this spire runs on, used to pick matching executables

tags.description:
Arbitrary operator-defined tags used for feature availability, placement
filtering, and discovery (e.g. "gpu", "eu-west", "high-mem").

ipPool.description:
Addresses this spire may bind shards to - each entry an individual IP or a
CIDR block (e.g. "10.0.0.5", "192.168.1.0/24"). Empty = any reported IP.

natsPrefix.description:
The NATS subject prefix this spire's agents listen on.
Derived from the hierarchy: `amp.tn.{tenant}.sp.{spireId}`.
Used by the orchestrator to address service requests to this spire.

allocatablePortRange.description:
The port pool available for shard assignment on this spire.
Stored as a serialised SparseRange string,
e.g. `1024:65535`. Defaults to the full unprivileged range.
Administrators can narrow this to avoid conflicts with host services.

acceptsDeployments.description:
Whether new shards may be deployed here. Disabling does not affect
shards already on the spire - it only removes it as a placement target.

maxShards.description: Maximum number of shards allowed on this spire. 0 = unlimited

defaultContainerMode.description:
Container mode applied to new shards created on this spire. Follows the host's detected
container runtime (see `ContainerModePolicy.SpireDefault`) until an operator sets it, on the
settings page or through the installer's server-runtime answer (`SpireSeed`), after which
bool SpireDefinition.DefaultContainerModeChosen keeps their choice. Individual shards can still be
changed after creation.

defaultContainerModeChosen.description:
Whether an operator has set ShardContainerMode SpireDefinition.DefaultContainerMode, through the settings surface or
the installer's seed.
Recorded rather than inferred from the value, because Native chosen on purpose and Native left
over from a host that had no runtime look identical. Once set it stays set.

preferredContainerMode.description:
Container runtime used when containerisation is forced (a mandated-container app, or a
containerised shard migrating in) rather than chosen. See `SpireSettings.PreferredContainerMode`.

defaultShardIpBinding.description:
The IP binding stamped on new shards' `$ApplicationIPBinding` at creation time. A literal
address, "0.0.0.0" (all interfaces), or string SpireDefinition.AutoFirstFromPool. Empty = use the app's
own template default. Only materially affects multi-IP-aware apps; others always bind 0.0.0.0.
Operators set this once per spire rather than repeating it on every shard.

createdAt.description: When this spire was first registered

panelPort.description:
The web port this machine's panel listens on, reported by the machine itself on every
heartbeat. Held back from every server placed there, because a server on it would take the
panel's firewall rule. The well-known number until the machine has reported.

busPort.description:
The client port of the message bus this machine runs, reported by the machine itself; 0 once
it has reported that it runs none. Held back like int SpireDefinition.PanelPort, and for the same
reason with a worse outcome: the bus's rule is host-only, and a server's would not be.

identityPublicKey.description:
The public half of the spire's persistent identity keypair (NKEY account public, e.g.
"A..."), published by the spire itself on self-registration. Peers verify cross-spire
principal-assertion tokens this spire signs against this key. Empty until the owning
host has registered with an identity.

role.description:
What this machine was added to do. Stamped at enrollment from the join file and deliberately
absent from SpireDefinition SpireDefinition.WithOperatorEditable(SpireDefinition patch) - the role decides whether the machine was ever
issued a shard signing key, so editing it afterwards could only ever produce a record that
disagreed with what the machine can actually do.

publicHost.description:
The public hostname or IP this spire is reachable at from the internet (e.g.
`vps.example.com` or `203.0.113.10`). SET = this spire is publicly routable: it can
FRONT port publications (players connect here), it's the endpoint tunnels dial, and shards
running ON it are already reachable at this address without any tunnel. EMPTY = private
(behind NAT / no public IP): can only be a tunnel BACK end, never a front. Operator-set,
since only the operator knows whether the machine truly has a routable address + open ports.

sftpEnabled.description:
Whether this spire runs its SFTP listener. Safe to leave on: authentication is by
registered public key only, so a listener nobody has given a key to cannot be entered.

sftpPort.description:
Port the SFTP listener binds. 2222 rather than 22 so it needs no privileged bind and does
not collide with the host's own sshd.

sftpBindAddress.description: Address to bind the SFTP listener to. Empty or unparseable means all interfaces

sftpHoneypot.description:
Catch SFTP scanners: advertise password authentication that is NEVER accepted, so a
             scanner reveals the username it is trying, and ban the address outright when that username
             is a known honeypot.

             The two halves are ONE setting because neither is worth anything alone. SSH only sends a
username once a client offers a credential we advertise; key-only means a password scanner
is refused during method negotiation and its username never reaches us, so the honeypot
list sits inert - it cannot fire on a name it never sees. Equally, advertising a password
path with no honeypot behind it is pure cost. AMP2 has these as two independent settings
and consequently has a combination that silently does nothing.No password is ever accepted, on any path, whatever this is set to: the advertisement is
bait, not a credential route. The trade is that a user with no key registered gets prompted
for a password that cannot work, rather than an immediate publickey refusal.

sftpIdleTimeoutSeconds.description:
Seconds an SFTP connection may sit idle before it is dropped. An abandoned session holds a
permission snapshot and a slot against the per-user limit, so it has to end on its own.
Floored at 30 wherever it is read - a shorter one would disconnect people mid-thought.

sftpMaxSessionsPerUser.description:
Concurrent SFTP connections one user may hold on this spire. Not a security boundary: it
stops one misconfigured client from opening connections until the process runs out of
them. Generous by default because ordinary clients legitimately open several at once (a
graphical client browsing while transferring is two or three on its own). 0 = unlimited.

shardSigningKeyPublic.description:
The public half of the SCOPED signing key this spire mints its own shards' credentials with.
Recorded so withdrawing the machine can drop the key from the account as well as revoking its
user: leave the key behind and a revoked machine can still mint itself a shard-shaped credential
and reconnect. Empty for a spire that predates scoped keys, or one on an unmanaged bus.

busUserPublicKey.description:
The public half of the bus key this spire authenticates with - the handle for revoking its
access. Recorded because without it we could not withdraw a machine at all: we would know it
was enrolled and have no idea which credential to cancel. Empty on an unmanaged bus.

captureAgentOutput.description:
Diagnostic: capture each shard agent's stdout/stderr on this machine and republish it as console
             output for the shard. Off by default and deliberately so - see
             `ShardAgentLauncher` for why leaving it on couples an agent's lifetime to the webapi's.

             It exists because an agent that dies before it can reach the bus has no other voice. Its output
is inherited by whatever console launched the webapi, which on a remote spire is a machine you
are not looking at - so the failure arrives as a bare exit code and nothing else.

logProcessLaunches.description:
Diagnostic. Writes every process launch (command line, working directory, and the environment
AMP set) into the shard's console. See `SpireSettings.LogProcessLaunches` for why this is
a spire setting rather than the developer-build toggle it started as.

isPubliclyRoutable.description: Convenience: whether this spire can front publications / be reached directly

isPublicEntryNode.description: Convenience: this machine relays and fronts the panel, and never hosts shards

canHostShards.description:
Whether this machine may host shards at all. A public entry node may not, ever, and that is
structural rather than a preference: it was never issued a shard signing key, so a shard placed
here could not be given a credential and its agent would be refused by the bus at connect.
Checking this at placement is what turns that into a sentence instead of a mystery.

acceptsNewShards.description:
Whether a new shard may be placed here: the machine is able to host at all, AND the operator is
currently letting it. Two different reasons with the same effect, kept apart because only one of
them is something the operator can change.

SpireDefinition.description:
Represents a physical or virtual machine that can host shard agents.
Spires are the execution layer - a shard is assigned to a spire and runs there.

KV key: `amp.tn.{tenant}.sp.{spireId}`

os.description: The operating system family the host runs

architecture.description: The host CPU architecture (e.g. x86_64, aarch64)

hardwareName.description: Board/hardware platform name where available (DMI / device-tree)

virtualization.description: The virtualization/container environment the host runs under, if any

reportedIps.description: All non-loopback IP addresses the host actually has, with per-address facts

installedJava.description:
Java runtimes installed on this host, for templates that need one and are not containerised.

             Reported by the spire rather than discovered on demand because the choice has to be made
before there is anything running to ask: at shard creation there is no agent, and while a
shard is stopped there may be none either. Containerised shards never consult this - their
Java comes from the image, and the setting gates to the container branch instead.

externalIp.description:
The address the internet sees this host as, or empty when it could not be determined. Every
other fact here is observable from the machine itself; this one is not, and no other spire can
work it out on this host's behalf - which is why it is reported rather than probed on demand.
A host behind NAT has no reachable address among IReadOnlyList<ReportedIpInfo> SpirePlatformInfo.ReportedIps, so this is the only
candidate a tunnel or a join file could offer it. Set by the reporter, not SpirePlatformInfo Detection.Detect(Action<string>? warn = null).

reachability.description:
How this host reaches the internet, which is what says whether string SpirePlatformInfo.ExternalIp is
usable: Direct means it is an address of this machine, Nat means it needs a port forward, and
Cgnat means no forward can help and only an outbound tunnel will work.

freeDiskMb.description: Free space on the drive the spire runs on, MB

totalDiskMb.description: Total capacity of the drive the spire runs on, MB (0 = unknown)

loadAvgPercent.description: System load as a percentage (Linux 1-minute load average times 100); -1 when unavailable

SpirePlatformInfo.description:
Hardware/OS facts a spire reports about itself, detected via
Detection and published to JetStream for dissemination.
Presentation/discoverability only - operators never edit this.

protocol.description: The port's protocol (for example TCP, UDP, or Both)

name.description: The port's human-readable name, falling back to its ref

shardId.description: The id of the shard that owns the port

shardName.description: The display name of the owning shard

ipBinding.description: The IP address the port is bound to

running.description: Whether the owning shard is currently running

listening.description: Whether the port was seen listening in the owner's latest metrics sample

conflict.description: Whether another shard claims the same port on an overlapping binding

SpirePortEntry.description: One expected port on a spire, with its owner and live status

SpireRole.description:
What a machine was added to do. Decided by the affordance the operator used to add it, stamped at
enrollment, and never operator-editable afterwards: a role that could be edited is not a guarantee,
and callers rely on this one.

spire.description: The spire definition, with its local flag stamped

online.description: Whether the spire is currently reporting heartbeats

lastSeen.description: When the spire was last seen, or null if never

version.description: The AMP version the spire last reported, or null if it never has

behind.description: True when the spire runs an older version than the installation and needs updating

installationVersion.description: The version the installation is on: the highest any spire reports

SpireRosterItem.description: One spire's entry in the cluster roster: its definition plus live liveness

startOnBoot.description: Whether the shard is started automatically when the spire boots

order.description: The shard's startup order (lower starts earlier)

SpireStartupEntry.description: One shard's place in a spire's boot sequence

startOnBoot.description: Whether the shard should start automatically when the spire boots

SpireStartupEntryBody.description: A submitted startup entry; list position sets the order, so only the boot flag is carried

spireId.description: The spire this state belongs to

online.description: True while the spire is considered reachable (recent heartbeat)

lastHeartbeat.description: Timestamp of the most recent heartbeat from the spire

shardCount.description: Number of shards currently assigned to this spire

cpuUsagePercent.description: Machine-wide CPU utilisation percentage at the last report

memoryUsedMb.description: Physical memory in use on the host, MB

memoryTotalMb.description: Total physical memory installed on the host, MB

networkInKBps.description:
Machine-level NIC throughput (all up, non-loopback/tunnel interfaces),
averaged over the reporter interval. Spire-wide, not per-shard - true
per-shard network accounting arrives with container mode.

networkOutKBps.description: Machine-level outbound NIC throughput, averaged over the reporter interval. See float SpireState.NetworkInKBps

diskActivePercent.description:
"Active time" of the drive backing the DEFAULT datastore, as a 0-100 percentage of
the reporter interval the disk had at least one I/O in flight - the same figure
Windows Task Manager shows as disk "Active time" / Linux iostat as "%util". A busy
indicator, not true saturation (an SSD can read 100% while still having headroom).
Null when it can't be sampled (no default datastore, counter unavailable, priming).

busLatencyMs.description: Round-trip latency (ms) from this spire to the NATS bus, measured each heartbeat

oneOf.description:
Reported hardware/OS facts for presentation and discovery - detected via
Detection and refreshed by the spire's heartbeat.

SpireState.description: Lightweight heartbeat state for a spire - written frequently by the spire itself

phase.description: Where the tunnel is in its bring-up (drives the progress readout as it comes up)

faultSpireId.description: For a fault phase, which end is at fault (so the UI can name the spire); else null

error.description:
The reason for an AgentRejected phase, or null: the agent's refusal of a rendered config, or the
at-fault spire's own refusal to render one (see string? SpireTunnel.FrontAgentError)

SpireTunnelStatus.description:
Live tunnel health, written by the FRONT spire's reconciler (a separate key so frequent
status writes never race the setup fields on the main record). "Up" is proved end-to-end:
an AMP-to-AMP UDP echo across the tunnel addresses, not just interface presence - so it
only goes green when the actual data path works.

id.description: The key's unique identifier

keyType.description: Key type as in authorized_keys, e.g. `ssh-ed25519`

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last authenticated an SFTP session, or null if never

expiresAt.description: When the key stops authenticating, or null if it does not expire

SshKeyDto.description: One of the caller's registered SSH public keys

targetDatastoreId.description: The datastore to copy the shard's working directory into

StartMigrationRequest.description: Request body for starting a same-spire datastore migration

SteamAnonymousLoginMode.description:
App.SteamUpdateAnonymousLogin - whether SteamCMD downloads need a real
Steam account (AMP 2 semantics; member names match template values).

vacBanned.description: Whether the account has a VAC (Valve Anti-Cheat) ban on record

vacBans.description: How many VAC bans; null when only the yes or no is known (the community profile)

gameBans.description: How many bans a game's own developer has issued; null when not known

daysSinceLastBan.description: Days since the most recent VAC or game ban; null when not known or none

communityBanned.description: Banned from the Steam Community; null when not known

tradeBanned.description: Banned from trading and the market

any.description: Whether there is any ban on record at all

SteamBans.description:
What Steam says about an account's bans. Bans are public whatever the profile's visibility, so
these are known for private profiles too.

personaName.description: The name they currently go by on Steam

avatarHash.description: Their avatar, as the hash Steam's image servers file it under; null for Steam's default

visibility.description: Who may see the profile's details

createdAt.description: When the account was made; only for public profiles

countryCode.description: The country they have put on the profile, lower-case ISO 3166-1; only for public profiles, and only when they set one

oneOf.description: Their bans; null when Steam did not answer

limited.description:
A limited account: one that has never spent money on Steam, so it cannot add friends or use the
market. Only the community profile says; null otherwise.

source.description: Where it came from: string SteamProfiles.FromWebApi or string SteamProfiles.FromCommunity

profileUrl.description: Their profile page, by id rather than custom address, so it survives a rename

SteamProfile.description:
What AMP learns about a Steam account from its Steam64 id: the public profile, from the Steam Web
API when a key is set and from the community profile page otherwise.

SteamVisibility.description: Who can see a Steam profile's details, as its owner has set it

id.description: Stable identity within the schedule - the run journal keys outcomes on it

StepIfStep.description: Branches on condition rows over the run context. Fully nestable

lane.description: "main", or "bg:{stepId}" for a background lane spawned by an un-awaited task

detail.description: Human detail: task output, error text, or which branch/case matched and why

StepOutcome.description: One step's outcome within a run - the journal entry the UI renders on the tree

notice.description: Why the step was refused, as a coded error the schedules tab translates

stepId.description: The refused step's id, set by the interpreter that ran it

StepRefusal.description:
A step AMP would not perform because a policy forbids it. The step is skipped rather than failed,
the rest of the run carries on, and the refusal is shown on the schedule and audited once.

id.description: Stable identity within the schedule - the run journal keys outcomes on it

StepStopStep.description: Stops the CURRENT lane cleanly (background lanes already running finish)

id.description: Stable identity within the schedule - the run journal keys outcomes on it

StepSwitchStep.description:
Evaluates string SwitchStep.Value once and runs the FIRST matching case (top-to-bottom), else
IReadOnlyList<Step> SwitchStep.Default. Sugar for an if/else-if chain, presented as a switch.

taskType.description: Catalog id of the task to run (e.g. "app.console.send", "shard.snapshot.create")

parameters.description: Per-parameter {@Var} template values, keyed by the catalog's parameter names

await.description:
For ASYNC task types only (catalog-declared): true = block this lane until the work
completes (flow continues downwards); false = start the work and continue immediately,
with IReadOnlyList<Step> TaskStep.OnSuccess/IReadOnlyList<Step> TaskStep.OnFailure running later in a concurrent
background lane ("sideways"). Ignored for synchronous task types.

onSuccess.description: Steps run after (and only if) the task succeeds

onFailure.description:
Steps run if the task fails. EMPTY = unhandled: FailurePolicy? TaskStep.FailureOverride (or the
task type's default policy) applies (Continue → run is marked CompletedWithErrors;
Abort → remaining steps are NotReached and the run is Failed). NON-empty = the user
handled the failure (like catch): the branch runs and the failure alone doesn't fail
the run.

oneOf.description:
Explicit user choice for what an unhandled failure does, overriding the task type's
default. An EXPLICIT Continue is stronger than the default: the failure is journaled
but deliberately does NOT mark the run (the user opted to swallow it - like an empty
catch); an explicit Abort fails the run as usual. Null = use the type's default.
Ignored when IReadOnlyList<Step> TaskStep.OnFailure is non-empty.

id.description: Stable identity within the schedule - the run journal keys outcomes on it

StepTaskStep.description:
Executes one task from the `TaskCatalog`. Parameters are {@Var} templates resolved
against the run context (the UI presents variables as chips; the braces syntax is wire-only).

SwitchCase.description: One case of a SwitchStep - any operator is allowed, not just equality

kind.description: Whether this is a full snapshot or a delta against its parent

content.description: Flags for which parts to capture: game state, base install data, and/or AMP configuration

name.description: Optional friendly name for the snapshot node

description.description: Optional longer description shown on the timeline

sticky.description: When true the snapshot is pinned and exempt from automatic retention pruning

TakeBody.description: Request body for taking a new snapshot

id.description: Stable task type id

category.description: Grouping used to organise tasks in the editor

isAsync.description: True when the task runs asynchronously (its completion is awaited by the runner)

defaultFailure.description: Default failure-handling mode as a string

parameters.description: The task's configurable parameters

TaskDescriptorDto.description: Describes one task type available to the editor

name.description: Parameter name

inputType.description: Input control hint the editor should render

required.description: Whether a value must be supplied

TaskParamDto.description: Describes one configurable parameter of a task

kind.description:
How this principal was established. The primary discriminator for
security queries - filter on `Kind == Impersonation` to find all
impersonation events without false-positives from scheduled jobs.

userId.description:
The direct actor. Null for PrincipalKind.System and
PrincipalKind.Scheduled where no human acted directly.

userDisplayName.description: Display name captured at the time of the action for audit readability

onBehalfOfUserId.description:
The user whose context this action belongs to when the direct actor is
            the system or a different user.
            * Scheduled: the user who created the schedule.
* Impersonation: the user being impersonated.

onBehalfOfUserDisplayName.description: Display name of the on-behalf-of user, captured at action time

systemSource.description:
Human-readable description of the initiating system component for
PrincipalKind.System and PrincipalKind.Scheduled
principals, e.g. `"Daily Backup"` or `"Instance Health Check"`.

TaskPrincipal.description:
Records who is responsible for an action and how that responsibility
was established. Every PrincipalKind value maps to exactly
one factory method so the fields are always populated consistently.

TemplateMatch.description: A template the candidate might be, and why

id.description:
Stable identifier for this source. Used as the local directory name and
as a prefix in slug collision resolution. Must be filesystem-safe.
Example: "official", "community-fork", "my-private-templates"

url.description:
Remote git URL (HTTPS or SSH), or `LOCAL/` for a development source.

             A URL beginning LOCAL/ means "this directory is mine, leave it alone": AMP never clones,
fetches or resets it, and reads whatever files are on disk. That is what makes it possible to
write a template in an editor and reload it, instead of having to commit and push to a git
remote for every change. Anything after the prefix names the directory under
string TemplateRepositoryOptions.BasePath; with nothing after it, the source
string TemplateSource.Id is used - so LOCAL/ alone is the shortest form that works.

isLocal.description:
Whether this source is a local development directory. Checked in every place that would
otherwise touch git, because running a hard reset over somebody's work-in-progress template
would destroy exactly the thing this feature exists to support.

localDirectoryName.description:
Directory name for a local source: whatever follows `LOCAL/`, else the source id. Any path
separators or traversal are stripped - the name must stay a single directory under BasePath.

isArchive.description:
Whether this source is a downloadable archive (`.zip`, `.tgz`, `.tar.gz` or
`.tar`) rather than a git repository. An archive source is fetched over HTTP(S) (or read
from a `file://` URL), unpacked into its own directory under
string TemplateRepositoryOptions.BasePath, and only re-downloaded when the server
reports it has changed. It has no branch.

branch.description: Branch to track. Defaults to "main". Meaningless for an archive source.

localPath.description:
Optional override for the local clone path. When null, the path is
derived as `{BasePath}/{Id}`.

priority.description:
Sources are merged in ascending priority order - higher number wins on
slug collision. The official repos take 0 and 1; user repos should use 10+.

disabled.description:
When true this source is skipped during sync/load without removing it
from configuration. Useful for temporarily disabling a repo.

TemplateSource.description:
Configuration for a single template source - one repository at one branch.
Multiple sources can be registered; their catalogues are merged in priority order.

termsVersion.description: The version accepted; the required version the agreement was fetched for

agreementHash.description: The hash of the agreement text shown. A hash that is no longer current is refused

attestation.description: The attestation exactly as it was ticked

locale.description: The panel's language at the time

TermsAcceptanceBody.description: The holder's acceptance of the current licence terms, as the panel collected it

servers.description:
How many servers they spent it on. More than one only for an id that means the same person
everywhere, a SteamID for instance; a name is only ever compared within one server.

online.description: They have a session still open: connected right now

timeZoneId.description:
IANA time zone id for DST-correct scheduling (e.g. "Europe/London").
Defaults to UTC. Explicit per schedule - "server timezone" is ambiguous
once there's more than one machine.

TriggerCronTrigger.description:
Fires at times described by a cron expression.
Uses Cronos for parsing - supports standard 5-field and extended 6-field
(with seconds) expressions. DST-safe via string CronTrigger.TimeZoneId.

id.description: Stable trigger type id

category.description: Grouping used to organise triggers in the editor

emits.description: Signals this trigger makes available to downstream conditions

label.description:
For a template-declared event, the template locale KEY naming it; empty for AMP's own triggers,
whose names live in AMP's own translations under `schedule.trigger.*`. Sent as a key rather
than resolved here so switching language re-renders without refetching the catalog, exactly as
setting labels already do.

description.description: The same, for the sentence explaining when it fires

TriggerDescriptorDto.description: Describes one trigger type available to the editor

TriggerEventTrigger.description:
Fires in response to a catalogued event on the bus. string EventTrigger.EventType is a
`TriggerCatalog` id (e.g. "player.joined"); the catalog maps it to the concrete NATS
subject for the schedule's shard and declares the values the event emits into the run
context. The event's agent-stamped EventId drives firing dedup across observers.

anchor.description:
Canonical anchor point for interval calculation - all nodes derive the
same `floor(now / interval) * interval` bucket from this.
Defaults to Unix epoch so intervals are globally aligned.

TriggerIntervalTrigger.description: Fires repeatedly on a fixed interval

backSpireId.description: Private spire that dials out to the front

slot.description: Deterministic slot (0-255) that drives the address pair and listen port

frontEndpointHost.description:
Public host the back spire dials, from the front spire's PublicHost setting - or, for a public
entry node still being set up, from the tunnel itself, since that machine has no record yet

interfaceName.description: WireGuard interface name shared by both ends

listenPort.description: UDP port the front spire listens on for this tunnel

frontAddress.description: Tunnel-internal address assigned to the front end

backAddress.description: Tunnel-internal address assigned to the back end

front.description: The front end's keys and system-agent state

back.description: The back end's keys and system-agent state

oneOf.description: Last reported link status, or null if neither end has reported yet

createdAt.description: When the tunnel record was created

permanentForEntryNode.description:
True for a public entry node's tunnel: it carries the bus rather than any route, so it exists
because that machine does and is not reference-counted off publications like every other tunnel.
The canvas needs to know, or it will describe a permanent wire as an unused one.

TunnelDto.description: A spire-to-spire WireGuard tunnel with both ends, addressing, and last reported status

spireId.description: Identifier of the spire this end runs on

spireName.description: Display name of the spire this end runs on

keyPublished.description: True once this end has generated and published its WireGuard public key

agentInstalled.description: True once the system agent has this end's WireGuard interface up

agentReachable.description: True while this spire's system agent is present and reporting. False means no agent has run here or it has stopped - and with no manual path, this end cannot come up

agentError.description: Why this end is not up when something refused it: its agent (e.g. an OS-reserved listen port) or its spire, which could not render the config (e.g. WireGuard missing); else null

TunnelEndDto.description: One end (front or back) of a tunnel, with the state of the system agent that brings it up

declaredHost.description:
Its PublicHost setting, or empty. When set it is simply what gets dialled and
Hosts is not a choice to make; when empty, one of them is adopted as it.

hosts.description: Candidate addresses, best-first, with the recommended one flagged

TunnelFrontDto.description: A spire that could be the public end of a tunnel, with the addresses it could terminate one on

TunnelPhase.description:
Where a tunnel is in its (continuously reconciled) bring-up. A single ladder both the tunnel
link on the canvas and every publication riding the tunnel report against, so "what is it doing
right now" reads the same everywhere. String-serialized so the API and UI speak phase NAMES.

message.description: English fallback, with the operating system's own words where it gave any

hideUnroutedShards.description:
Hide servers with no route on the networking canvas. Off by default, because an unrouted
server is the thing you drag onto a front to route it - but an installation past a certain
size wants it on, and having to set it again on every visit is the sort of small friction
that makes a screen tiring to use.

hidePrivatePorts.description:
Hide ports the application does not expose publicly on the networking canvas. On by default:
a private port cannot be published, so on the screen whose whole job is publishing ports it
is a row of things you are not allowed to touch. Off for the operator who wants the full
picture of what a server has open.

fileDetailsWidth.description:
Width in CSS pixels of the file manager's details pane, as left by the user's last drag of
the splitter. Null = the default width. The client clamps on read, so an out-of-range value
stored here is harmless.

oneOf.description: The user's self-reported familiarity with AMP, captured at onboarding. Null = never asked.

showTutorials.description:
Whether guided tutorials are offered at all: the master switch behind every "Show Tutorial"
button. Defaulted from UserExperienceLevel? UserPreferences.AmpExperience at onboarding (on for new / returning
users, off for the experienced) and then user-adjustable from the profile dialog.

tutorialPromptDismissed.description:
Whether the user has answered "Never ask again" to the offer of the getting-started
tutorial, or has already finished it. Suppresses the automatic prompt only; the per-screen
"Show Tutorial" buttons are governed by bool? UserPreferences.ShowTutorials and stay available.
Null/false means the prompt is still offered, which is what "Ask me next time" leaves behind.

tutorialsCompleted.description:
Ids of the tutorials the user has run to the end, so a "Show Tutorial" button can present
itself as a replay and the getting-started offer stops once it has been taken.

accessibilityHintsEnabled.description:
Whether to surface extra accessibility instructions in the UI (e.g. how to operate the
keyboard-driven confirm slider). The accommodations themselves are always available; this
only governs whether the explanatory hints are shown. Null = never asked.

onboardingCompleted.description:
Whether the user has completed the first-login onboarding wizard. Null/false means the wizard
should be shown on next login, regardless of how the account was created (invite, API, setup).

reducedMotion.description:
Whether to reduce non-essential UI animation. This is IN ADDITION to the browser's
prefers-reduced-motion media query, not a replacement: the OS setting is machine-wide and
all-or-nothing, so this lets a user ask for calmer motion in AMP alone. Either source turning
it on reduces motion. Null/false means follow the OS only.

analyticsEnabled.description:
Whether the user consents to anonymous product analytics (used later to drive Plausible).
Opt-in: null/false means no analytics. Distinct from the system-level crash-report setting.

streamerMode.description:
Streamer Mode: blur every place the panel deliberately shows an IP address, so a stream or a
recording of the screen never carries one. Console and log text is left alone. Null/false
means addresses are shown plainly.

oneOf.description:
Whether clock times are written 12- or 24-hour. Null = TimeFormat.System,
i.e. whatever the user's language implies. Separate from string? UserPreferences.Locale because the
two are genuinely independent: plenty of people read English and write the time as 21:30.

UserPreferences.description:
Per-user preferences stored in NATS KV.
All fields are optional - absent fields mean "use the system default".

KV key: `amp.tn.{tenant}.usr.{userId}.prefs`

Design principles:
  - One record per user, updated with PATCH semantics (only changed fields written).
  - All fields are nullable so callers can distinguish "explicitly set to X"
    from "never set" without magic sentinel values.
  - New preference fields are additive - no migration needed.

VersionCandidate.description: One selectable version produced by a VersionSource

candidates.description: Versions the user can pick from, already ordered

fetchedAt.description: When this was last successfully read from upstream

failureReason.description:
Why the last refresh failed, when it did. Candidates may still be
    populated - a stale list plus an explanation beats an empty one.

fromCache.description: Whether this was served from cache without going upstream

age.description: How old the data is, for the UI to say "this list may be out of date"

VersionCandidateList.description: A cached candidate list, as stored and as served

VersionSortOrder.description: How candidates are ordered before they reach the user

id.description: Identifies this source; a setting names it to be fed from it

url.description: The single upstream document, for the common case. Ignored when List<VersionSourceDocument> VersionSource.Documents is set.

documents.description: Several upstream documents merged into one list, in order

select.description: Path selecting the candidate nodes (JSONPath or XPath per VersionSourceFormat VersionSource.Format)

value.description: Path WITHIN a candidate giving the stored value. Empty or `$` means the node itself.

display.description: Path within a candidate giving the display string. Empty falls back to the value.

fields.description:
Extra named values pulled from each candidate, as `name -> path within the candidate`.
These become `{{Setting.name}}` tokens once a candidate is selected, which is how a
second-hop URL (Mojang) or a download filename (Paper) reaches the update stage.

where.description:
Values a candidate must carry to enter the list, as `field name -> required value`
over Dictionary<string, string> VersionSource.Fields. Applied as the list is read, so a candidate that fails it is
never cached, never offered and never what string VersionSelection.Latest means:
Mojang's manifest lists snapshots first, and the latest Vanilla Minecraft has to be the
latest release. A candidate without the field does not match; values compare exactly.

urlTemplate.description:
Builds the download URL from a candidate. Tokens are `{value}`, `{display}` and
any Dictionary<string, string> VersionSource.Fields name. The result is exposed as the reserved
`downloadUrl` field, so an update stage is just
`FetchURL` of `{{Setting.downloadUrl}}` and no new stage type is needed.

sort.description: Ordering applied before the list is shown

cacheMinutes.description: How long a fetched list stays fresh for DISPLAY. Resolution tolerates any age.

dependsOn.description:
Settings whose values this source's URLs interpolate. Load-bearing in three places: it keys
the cache, it invalidates this source when one of them changes, and it tells the UI which
dependent dropdowns to clear. A source with dependencies is not evaluated until they all
have values.

VersionSource.description:
A list of installable versions read from an upstream manifest, so a template can offer a real
             dropdown instead of asking the user to type a version string.

             Each candidate carries three things: the string VersionSource.Value that gets stored, the
string VersionSource.Display string the user picks from, and a bag of named Dictionary<string, string> VersionSource.Fields. The
selected candidate's fields become {{Setting.field}} tokens usable anywhere a token
already is - another source's URL, a download URL template, an update stage's arguments. That
one rule is what lets a single mechanism cover every upstream, including the ones that need a
second request to find the actual download.See docs/version-sources.md for the reasoning, including why a value the upstream
already publishes whole (Forge's 1.20.1-47.2.0) is kept whole rather than split.

url.description: Where to fetch it. May carry `{{Setting}}` tokens (see List<string> VersionSource.DependsOn)

urlTemplate.description:
Download URL for candidates from THIS document, overriding the source's own template.
Empty means use the source's.

VersionSourceDocument.description:
One upstream document a VersionSource reads. Most sources have exactly one and
declare it inline on the source; the list exists for upstreams that split the same logical
list across several documents, which is how NeoForge's old and new artifact naming is handled
without having to work out afterwards which naming a given version used.

VersionSourceFormat.description: How a version manifest is encoded, which decides the path language used to read it

VirtualizationType.description:
The virtualization or container environment a host was detected to be running under,
or VirtualizationType.None for bare metal. Reported for presentation and diagnostics.

WithheldParameter.description: A step parameter whose value a response withholds

shardId.description: The server the rule was derived for

kind.description: Which of AMP's own listeners holds the number

WithheldPortRule.description:
A server-derived firewall rule withheld because AMP itself holds the number. The server behind it
is unreachable on that port until it is moved, and nothing outside this record says why.

Bearer.description: The session token AMP issues at sign-in.
